As at Jerusalem the gift worked its effect upon the Jews gathered at the feast from every part of the empire, so now the Spirit, given in this center of Gentile activity, would have a like result, that the amazement of the people at such a power might attract attention to the message and gain converts to Christ. “Thus they were qualified to labor as missionaries in Ephesus and its vicinity, and also to go forth to proclaim the gospel in Asia Minor” (EGW RH Aug. 31, 1911). Prophesied. Rather, “began prophesying.” This signifies a more convicting presentation of the gospel, bringing in an exposition of OT prophecy and a greater power of preaching. The foretelling of future events would be of little help to the cause of Christ at this time and is not necessarily meant by this word.
6.zh:
保羅按手在他們頭上，聖靈便降在他們身上，他們就說方言，又說預言（或作：又講道）

**按手。**見徒6:6註釋。
**聖靈便降在他們身上。**這是《使徒行傳》所記載凡受洗的人所共有的經驗。聖靈這次的下降，是為一項大工作準備。這項工作是要把這座完全獻給底米丟女神（黛安娜）的以弗所，變成一個基督所充分征服的地方，變成這個地區基督徒生活的中心，達數世紀之久。
**就說方言。**或“開口說方言”。就像五旬節聖靈沛降那樣。在耶路撒冷，聖靈的恩賜曾影響了從帝國各地聚集來過節的猶太人，現在聖靈在這個異教活動中心的降下，也產生了類似的效果。人們對這種能力的驚訝，會吸引他們關注信息，併為基督贏得信徒。“他們就這樣獲得資格，在以弗所和周邊地區擔任傳道士，並前往小亞細亞傳揚福音”（懷愛倫《評論與通訊》1911年8月31日）。
**又說預言（或作：**又講道）。或“開始說預言”。這標誌著福音更有說服力的傳播，《舊約》預言的詮釋，和更大的傳道能力。預言將來的事件對於當時的聖工沒有幫助，所以不是這句話所指的意思。

5.en: When they heard this. “This” is supplied by the translators, and probably should be omitted. What these converts heard, doubtless, was not the mere statement that Jesus was the Messiah, but the arguments, with OT scriptures, by which Paul proved this to be true, showing that in Him the OT was fulfilled. Though the description here is brief, their conviction was not necessarily sudden or without full instruction. In the name. Rather, “into the name.” for the significance of “name” see on chs. 3:16; 4:12. Here is an example of individuals rebaptized upon the reception of vital truth, new to them. But this gives no warrant for frequent rebaptizings. Rebaptism should rarely be administered. The cleansing from sins that come into the Christian’s experience in his daily walk in a sinful world is provided by the forgiving grace of God through Christ (1 John 1:9; 2:1, 2) and witnessed to by the ordinance of foot washing, which symbolizes a washing away of sin (John 13:4–10). When one has been baptized into Christ, rebaptism is called for only if there has been a definite apostasy from the beliefs and standards that fellowship with Christ requires. Exceptions to this general rule would be cases like the one here described. Baptism into the name of Christ is the pledge of entrance into the covenant of salvation, and is intended to be a permanent and abiding experience.
5.zh:
他們聽見這話，就奉主耶穌的名受洗。

**他們聽見這話。**“這”是譯者加的，或許可以刪除。這些信徒所聽到的，無疑不僅是說耶穌是彌賽亞的話，而且是保羅以《舊約》為據，證明這是真的，顯明《舊約》應驗在祂身上。雖然這裡的句子很簡潔，但他們不一定未經充分指教就立即相信了。
**就奉主耶穌的名。**關於“名”的意義，見徒3:16；4:12註釋。這是個人接受重要新真理時重新受洗的一個例子，但不能作為多次重新受洗的依據。重新洗禮要慎行。基督徒每天行走在罪惡的世界中所沾罪惡的潔淨，是依靠上帝藉著基督所賜的赦罪之恩（約壹1:9；2:1,2），由象徵洗除罪惡的洗腳禮所見證（約13:4-10）。當一個人受洗歸入基督之後，只有在公然背離基督徒信仰和準則的情況下，才需要重新受洗。除了這條總的原則，還有象本節所描述的例外。奉基督的名受洗，就是保證信守救恩的約，要成為一種永久常存的經驗。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第285頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–6節）**。《使徒行述》第283頁。

9.en: Divers were hardened, and believed not. Or, “Some were growing hardened and disobedient.” See on ch. 14:2. Spake evil of that way. That is, of Christians and Christianity. The unbelieving Jews acted at Ephesus as their fellows had at Thessalonica. They probably displayed their hatred of Paul by attempting to turn the Gentiles against him. People of the lower classes were always ready to riot. He departed. That is, he ceased to take part in the public services of the synagogue. Separated the disciples. That is, the Christian part of the congregation in the synagogue was withdrawn, along with any of the Jews who had become interested in his teaching. This is the first recorded time when the entire group of Christian believers severed their connection with the Jewish synagogue. The process of withdrawal must have been accelerated during the period of the Jewish wars, A.D. 68–135, when it was not only uncomfortable, but in some places actually dangerous, to be associated with Jews (see Vol. V, p. 80). Disputing. Some textual evidence may be cited (cf. p. 10) for the alternate reading, “disputing daily in school of one Tyrannus from the fifth hour to the tenth.” Scholars disagree as to whether this reading is to be considered original. If it is, it suggests the interesting thought that since the period from the fifth to the tenth hour (about 11 A.M. to 4 P.M. ) is the siesta hour in Eastern countries, Paul would have used this building for his teaching during “off hours,” when Tyrannus’ school would not have been in session. Daily. How often Paul had taught in the synagogue during his first three months at Ephesus cannot be known, though he was there doubtless each Sabbath, and perhaps oftener. Now, at least, he entered upon an intensive program of public evangelism, to which he devoted part, at least, of each day. Presumably he continued at the same time to earn his own living (see on v. 8). The school. Gr. scholē. This word has an interesting history. Originally it meant “leisure”; then it was applied to leisure as bestowed upon learned discussion and study; then, as here, to the place in which the study was pursued. Lastly it became a collective term for the followers of a particular teacher, as “the school of Zeno.” In this verse it probably indicates a lecture room, which, as the private property of the owner, was lent or rented to the apostle. One Tyrannus. Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) omitting the word “one,” which suggests that Tyrannus may have been a well-known person. Of this man nothing more is known with certainty. He may have been a teacher of philosophy or rhetoric, but if so he could hardly have been an entirely unconverted heathen. Such a person would not likely permit his classroom to be used by a teacher of a new faith that was ridiculed in certain circles (see ch. 17:32). Some therefore think this was a Jewish school, a Beth–Hammidrash, in which Paul’s Jewish hearers would be more likely to assemble. The listeners evidently were partly Jews and partly Greeks. No doubt there were enough Jews in Ephesus to make such “schools” necessary for their education, and the leader of such a school would very readily adopt a Gentile name in addition to his Jewish one. So Tyrannus may possibly have been a Jew.
9.zh:
後來，有些人心裡剛硬不信，在眾人面前毀謗這道，保羅就離開他們，也叫門徒與他們分離，便在推喇奴的學房天天辯論。

**有些人心裡剛硬不信。**或“有些人心裡剛硬，並不順從”。見徒14:2註釋。
**在眾人面前毀謗這道。**指毀謗基督徒和基督教。不信的猶太人在以弗所的活動就像他們在帖撒羅尼迦的同胞一樣。他們可能試圖煽動外邦人來攻擊保羅，以發洩他們對保羅的仇恨。下層階級的百姓是很願意鬧事的。
**保羅就離開他們。**指保羅不再參加會堂的公共崇拜。
**叫門徒與他們分離。**即基督徒和一切對他的教訓感興趣的猶太人退出會堂。這是第一次記載整個基督徒團體與猶太會堂脫離關係。撤離的過程在公元68-135年猶太人戰爭期間一定加快了。因為那時與猶太人聯合不僅不愉快，而且在有些地方還很危險（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷五第80頁）。
**推喇奴。**暗示推喇奴可能是一個著名的人物。關於這個人沒有什麼確切的信息。他可能是一個哲學教師或修辭教師。但若是這樣，他就不大可能是一個完全沒有悔改的外邦人。否則他不會讓一個新信仰的教師使用他的教室餓；況且這種信仰在某些圈子裡還是受人嘲笑的（見徒17:32）。有文本為“一個推喇奴”。
因此有人認為這是一個猶太人的學校（“Beth-Hammidrash”），保羅的猶太人聽眾更有可在裡面會聚。聽眾顯然有一部分人是猶太人，有一部分人是希臘人。無疑在以弗所有足夠的猶太人，可以開設這樣的“學房”從事教育工作。這種學房的負責人除了自己的猶太名字之外，很可能再取一個外邦名字。所以“推喇奴”可能是一名猶太人。
**學房。**scholē。該詞有一段有趣的歷史。它原指“閒暇”，後指進行學術討論和研究的閒暇時間；再後來如這裡指進行學習的場所。最後變成一個集體名詞，指某一個教師門下的學生，例如“齊諾學派”。該詞在本節可能指一個空閒的房子，為私人所有，借給或租給使徒。
**天天。**不知道保羅在以弗所的頭三個月時間裡去會堂教導的頻率如何。他每個安息日無疑是去的。也許其他時間也有去。現在保羅開始進行一個比較集中的公眾佈道項目，每天至少要投入一部分工夫。這這段時間裡，保羅可能繼續靠手藝謀生（見第8節註釋）。
**辯論。**有文本為“在推喇奴的學房天天辯論，從五時到十時”。關於這樣的句子是否原文就有，學者們有不同的意見。若是有的話，就引出了一個有趣的推測，因為從五時到十時（約從上午11點鐘到下午4點）是東方國家午休的時間。保羅可能利用推喇奴學房課餘不上課的時間教導真理。

19.en: Many of them. The clause reads literally, “Many of those who were practicing superfluous things,” meaning the superstitious, magical arts. These arts were almost a specialty in Ephesus. The magicians and astrologers were about in great numbers, and carried on a brisk trade in charms, books of divination, and rules for interpreting dreams. The so-called “Ephesian spells,” or “Ephesian writings” (Ephesian grammata), were small slips of parchment kept in silk bags, and on these slips were written archaic words of obscure meaning. Clement of Alexandria lists these words (Stromata v. 8), and despite their being so obscure as to defy linguistic analysis he interprets them as meaning darkness and light, the earth and the year, the sun and truth. They doubtless represent a survival of the old Phrygian nature cult, which antedated the Greek goddess Artemis, and which was later combined with superstitions that drifted in from other religions. Brought their books together. This must mean the gathering together of the papers upon which the spells and incantations had been written, the “Ephesian writings,” and the books put out as treatises upon these occult “arts.” Some of these “writings” were allegedly of great antiquity, perhaps going as far back as the days of Moses. Probably also charms, or amulets, were brought. Burned them. There appears to be a relation between this burning and the healings through Paul that were followed by the overcoming of the pretended exorcists by the demon (see vs. 12, 16). Those who “believed” sensed clearly that the power of Christianity was superior to “curious arts.” Charms, mystic names, formulas, and “letters” stood exposed as empty pretenses. Accordingly, the written incantations, and the treatises containing them, were burned. The Greek verb form may imply either continuous burning, over a period of hours, as book after book was thrown on, or repeated acts of burning. Such a demonstration must have attracted considerable notice. They counted the price. The sacrifice made by the believers consisted not only of the cost of the books, which is named by Luke, but also of the loss of potential income, which they might have received from practicing the “curious arts.” Fifty thousand pieces of silver. Since this dramatic burning of books, esteemed by so many to be valuable, took place in the midst of a Greek population, it is probable that Luke was thinking of the Greek drachmas as the “pieces of silver.” If so, 50,000 of these united would be worth a little over $5,000. Since, however, the drachma was about equivalent to a day’s wages at that time, it will be seen that the then-current market value was far greater than would be suggested by the equivalent figure in dollars. Some of the books would undoubtedly have brought a high price, if offered for sale. See Vol. V, p. 49.
19.zh:
平素行邪術的，也有許多人把書拿來，堆積在眾人面前焚燒。他們算計書價，便知道共合五萬塊錢。

**平素行邪術的，也有許多人。**“邪術”意為迷信的法術。這些法術幾乎是以弗所的專長。法術師和占星家到處可見，為數眾多，進行符咒，預言書籍和解夢規則的繁忙交易。所謂“以弗所符咒”或“以弗所著作”（Ephesian grammata）是放在絲綢袋裡的羊皮小紙片，上面寫著晦澀不明的古老文字。亞歷山大的革利免列出了這些文字（Stromata v.8）。儘管這些文字意義含糊，，很難進行語言分析，革利免仍將它們解釋出來，意思是黑暗與光明，地球與年，太陽與真理。它們無疑是古代佛裡吉亞人自然宗教的遺蹟。它先於希臘的女神亞底米，後來與其他宗教的迷信混合在一起。
**把書拿來。**一定是指把寫有符咒的紙張，“以弗所著作”和有關巫術的書籍都集中起來。有些“著作”被視為珍貴的古董，也許可以追溯到摩西的時代。也許還帶來一些法術和護身符之類的書。
**焚燒。**行騙的驅魔師被魔鬼制伏以後，保羅治好了病人。焚燒邪術的書籍可能與這件事有關（見第12,16節）。“已經信的”人清楚地意識到基督教的能力超過“法術”。字符，神秘的名字，咒語和文書都暴露出虛假的本質。因此書面的咒語和法術的書籍都燒掉了。原文動詞的形式或暗示一次性焚燒，持續好幾個小時，一本一本書扔進去，或分幾次焚燒。這樣的行動一定吸引許多人關注。
**他們算計書價。**信徒的犧牲不僅包括書的價值，還包括損失他們靠行“邪術”而獲的潛在收入。
**共合五萬塊錢。**許多人估計這些書的價值很高。由於這場轟動性的焚書事件發生在希臘人中間，路加所指的“錢“可能是古希臘的銀幣。若是這樣， 50,000塊錢的價值就稍超過5,000美元。然而當時的一塊希臘銀幣相當於一天的工資，可見當時貨幣市場價值要遠遠超過我們今天按照美元計算出來的數字。其中一些書如果出售的話，無疑能賣出很高的價格。見《SDA聖經註釋》卷五第49頁。

33.en: They drew. Textual evidence favors (cf. p. 10) a variant reading which, though difficult to translate, is here probably best rendered, “they prompted.” With this reading the whole clause may be translated, “some of the crowd prompted Alexander” (RSV). Alexander. This Alexander was perhaps the “coppersmith” (2 Tim. 4:14) who worked “much evil” against the apostle in Ephesus. Made his defence. Gr. apologeomai, “to justify oneself [in the eyes of another].” The uproar was essentially pagan—Demetrius was a heathen idol maker, and his charge against Paul would have significance only to pagans. Doubtless Paul was known to be a Jew, and the Ephesian Jews, who also refused to worship Artemis, apparently were fearful lest the riot become an anti-Semitic pogrom. Evidently, then, the “defence” that Alexander sought to make was to dissociate the Ephesian Jews from any connection with Paul and his company, in the pagan mind.
33.zh:
有人把亞力山大從眾人中帶出來，猶太人推他往前，亞力山大就擺手，要向百姓分訴；

**亞歷山大。**這位亞歷山大可能就是在以弗所“多多地害”保羅的“銅匠”（提後4:14）。
**帶出來。**有文本為 “他們慫恿”。
**向百姓分訴。**apologeomai。進行騷亂的基本上都是異教徒──底米丟是異教偶像的製作者。他對於保羅的指控只對於外邦人有意義。他們無疑知道保羅是猶太人。以弗所的猶太人也是拒絕敬拜亞底米的。他們顯然害怕這場騷亂會演變成針對猶太人的屠殺。亞歷山大的“分訴”是要對異教徒說明，保羅和他的同伴與以弗所的猶太人是沒有關係的。
**懷愛倫註釋**。見提後4：3-14懷愛倫註釋。

28.en: Full of wrath. Demetrius had appealed to the people in such a way as to excite them more and more by each additional argument. Appeals were skillfully made to their self-interest first, and then to their pride and superstition. Cried out. Or, “they began crying out.” The tense implies the beginning of continued or repeated action. Great is Diana. The mob, incited by Demetrius’ oratory, apparently took up this cry as a rallying slogan, shouting it over and over again as their excitement grew and their better senses were lost in a flood of mass emotion.
28.zh:
眾人聽見，就怒氣填胸，喊著說：大哉，以弗所人的亞底米啊！

**怒氣填胸。**底米丟不斷地添油加醋，煽動百姓，令他們越來越生氣。挑撥的話先觸動他們的個人利益，然後觸及他們的驕傲和迷信。
**喊著說。**或“開始呼喊”。動詞的時態暗示持續動作的開始。
大哉，…亞底米啊！在底米丟演講的煽動下，暴徒們把這句話當作行動的口號，一遍又一遍地呼喊，情緒越來越激動，在群情激昂的狀態下喪失了理性。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第286頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（28–31節）**。《使徒行述》第293頁。

1.en: While Apollos was at Corinth. The parenthesis concerning Apollos having ended, the record now returns to Paul. Apollos found in Corinth a very effective center for his work in Achaia, and seems to have made this his headquarters for the time. At this juncture Paul was proceeding westward (ch. 18:23) across Asia Minor toward Ephesus. Upper coasts. Or, “upper regions” of a larger area (see on ch. 13:50). These lay farther inland. The apostle’s journey was probably through Lycaonia, Galatia, and Phrygia, which he had visited before. Came to Ephesus. This visit was in fulfillment of the promise made by him when he left the city before (ch. 18:21). Certain disciples. They are called “disciples” because, like Apollos, they had learned some things concerning Jesus, upon the basis of which they had been drawn to listen to Paul, who could teach them more.
1.zh:
亞波羅在哥林多的時候，保羅經過了上邊一帶地方，就來到以弗所；在那裡遇見幾個門徒，

**亞波羅在哥林多的時候。**關於亞波羅的插敘結束了。記錄回到了保羅身上。亞波羅在哥林多找到了他在亞該亞有效開展工作的基地，似乎一時將它當作他的總部。這時保羅繼續西進（徒18:23），穿過小亞細亞，前往以弗所。
**上邊的一帶地方。**或“海岸上方”，是一片很大的區域（見徒13:50註釋），屬於內陸地區。保羅的行程可能經過他以前曾拜訪的呂高尼、加拉太和弗呂家。
**就來到以弗所。**這次訪問是履行他以前離開這裡時的承諾（徒18:21）。
**幾個門徒。**他們被成為“門徒”，是因為他們像亞波羅一樣，曾學了一些有關耶穌的知識，在這樣的基礎上，被吸引來聽保羅教導他們更多的真理。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第281頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–41節）**。《使徒行述》第281-297頁。

3.en: Unto what? Rather, “Into what?” (see on chs. 2:41; 8:38). The NT phrase is “baptize in,” or “baptize into,” to express the close union with God into which men are brought by the symbolic act of immersion. The answers of the men so far had shown incomplete instruction, which fell short of what candidates for baptism ordinarily received, and also an incomplete spiritual experience, corresponding with their lack of knowledge. They were doubtless unaware of their own lack, and probably considered themselves fully qualified to belong to the congregation of believers. Unto John’s baptism. Rather, “into John’s baptism.” The baptism may possibly have been by Apollos, administered before he had had his fuller instruction by Aquila and Priscilla, or by someone like him. Except for v. 4 this is the last NT reference to John the Baptist.
3.zh:
保羅說：這樣，你們受的是什麼洗呢？他們說：是約翰的洗。

**你們受的是什麼。**（見徒2:41；8:38註釋）。《新約》中的“受洗”是指藉著浸入水中的象徵性舉動，與上帝建立密切的聯合。這些人的回答說明他們所受的指導是不充分的，因著這種缺乏，他們不具備領浸者所應有的知識，和完善的屬靈經歷。他們無疑不知道自己的缺乏，可能覺得自己有足夠的資格從屬於信徒的會眾。
**是約翰的洗。**可能是亞波羅施行的洗禮；那是在他領受了百基拉和亞居拉更詳細的指導之前。或者是像亞波羅那樣的人施行的洗禮。除了本章第4節之外，這是《新約》最後一次提到施洗約翰。

31.en: Chief of Asia. Or, “Asiarchs.” This official title was applied to those who were selected annually from the chief cities of the province to preside at the religious festivals and public games. Ten Asiarchs were selected from the larger number of city representatives, and one of these the proconsul nominated as president. Their duties led them to the various cities where and when games or festivals were held. Since they were connected with the theater and the worship of Artemis, as well as the worship of the emperor, the Asiarchs were probably informed of the riot and its cause. The references to the Passover service in 1 Cor. 5:6–8 have been thought to suggest that Paul wrote that epistle about Passover time. As he probably left Corinth not many weeks later (2 Corinthians was written from Macedonia), and as his departure was soon after the uprising (Acts 20:1), it may well have been that the uprising occurred shortly after Passover, in the spring. In that event the people were keeping, or anticipating, the great festival in honor of Artemis, in the month named after her, Artemision (April–May). As a result they were more susceptible to Demetrius’ appeal. At that season of the year the Asiarchs would also be in Ephesus. His friends. The tact and courtesy of Paul’s zeal and boldness apparently won the attention and respect of men in authority. This was true of the Asiarchs, as at other times of Sergius Paulus (ch. 13:7–12), Gallio (ch. 18:14–17), Festus (ch. 25:9–12), Agrippa (ch. 26:28, 32), and the centurion Julius (ch. 27:3, 43). The Asiarchs gave the same advice as that of the disciples, though from different motives. They realized that his presence could not help but excite the passions of the crowd still further. Not adventure himself. Or, “not venture.” These friendly officials took a personal interest in Paul’s safety.
31.zh:
還有亞西亞幾位首領，是保羅的朋友，打發人來勸他，不要冒險到戲園裡去。

**亞細亞的幾位首領。**指一年一度從行省的主要城市裡選出來主持宗教節期和公眾競賽的官員。先從更多的城市代表中選出十人，然後地方總督（方伯）從中任命一個人擔任主席。他們的責任是到舉辦節期或競賽的城市去。他們與戲園，亞底米的崇拜和皇帝的敬拜有關係，可能知道這場暴亂及其原因。林前5:6-8 提到逾越節的崇事，被認為保羅寫這封書信大約是在逾越節的時候。短短几周之後，保羅可能離開了哥林多（《哥林多後書》是在馬其頓寫的），他的離開是在這次動亂之後不久（徒20:1），這次的動亂可能是在逾越節之後不久發生的，是在春天。在這個事件中，百姓正在遵守或期待崇拜亞底米的大節期，時間是按她的名字命名的亞底米月（四月至五月）。結果他們便更容易受底米丟的煽動了。在每年的這個季節，這些首領也在以弗所。
**保羅的朋友。**保羅熱心和勇敢所表現出來的機智和謙恭，顯然贏得了當權者的關注和尊重。那幾位首領也是如此。還有其他場合的士求保羅（徒13:7-12），迦流（徒18:14-17），非斯都（徒25:9-12），亞基帕（徒26:28,32）和百夫長猶流（徒27:3,43）。首領們的忠告與門徒是一樣的，儘管動機不同。他們意識到保羅的出場非但無濟於事，反而會激化群眾的情緒。
**不要冒險。**這些友好的官員關心保羅的安全。

35.en: Townclerk. Gr. grammateus, translated “scribe” in the Gospels. He was custodian of the city records, and was a highly influential man in Ephesus. Through him all public communications were made to the city and replies given. This part of his duties led to the English title “townclerk.” The Greek title appears in many inscriptions from Ephesus, often in conjunction with those of the Asiarchs, all of whom were citizens of Ephesus, and the proconsul. The language of the public officer is as gravely cautious as that of Demetrius had been inflammatory. Like the Asiarchs, he looked upon Paul and his companions with obvious respect. He was no fanatic, and had no intention of becoming a persecutor. He did not oppose the multitude, but sought to soothe them with a profession of fondness for their religion. Worshipper. Gr. neōkoros, literally, “temple sweeper,” and, by extension, any devotee of a god and its shrine. The whole city is represented as consecrated to the service of the goddess. The word neōkoros is found on coins from Asia Minor, expressive of the devotion of certain cities to a god or an emperor. The people of Ephesus looked to Artemis as their guardian and protector. On one inscription the city claims the honor of being her “nurse.” Great goddess Diana. Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the omission of the word “goddess.” In some of the inscriptions of Ephesus she is described as “the greatest,” “the most high.” Image which fell down from Jupiter. Gr. Diopetēs, “fallen from Zeus [or heaven]”— a name often given to old, prehistoric images, as for example, to that of Pallas Athene at Athens and to the Palladium of the Trojans (Virgil Aeneid ii. 183). Here the word may have had a more literal meaning as applied to a meteoric stone that was worshiped in its original form or used in the earliest sculpture. Thus it may not refer to Artemis’ image (see on v. 24), which, according to various ancient authors, was made, not of stone, but of olivewood, ebony, cedarwood, or wood of the vine, if not of gold.
35.zh:
那城裡的書記安撫了眾人，就說：以弗所人哪，誰不知道以弗所人的城是看守大亞底米的廟和從丟斯那裡落下來的像呢？

**書記。**grammateus，在福音書中譯為“文士”。他是城市記錄的保管員，在以弗所頗具影響力。所有的公共通信都是通過他傳到市裡並獲得答覆的。以弗所的許多碑銘上有這個希臘的官銜，往往同來自以弗所市民的“首領”的官銜，以及“方伯”的官銜聯繫在一起。這位公職人員的話非常謹慎，不象底米丟那樣具有煽動性。他象“首領”們一樣，十分尊重保羅和他的同伴。他不是狂熱之徒，不想成為迫害者。他沒有反對群眾，卻設法以維護他們宗教的姿態安撫他們。
**看守。**neōkoros，直譯是“神廟清掃者”，引申為敬奉神明或神龕的人。全城都是奉獻侍奉女神的。小亞細亞出土的硬幣上有neōkoros的字樣，表達了對神明或皇帝的忠誠。以弗所的百姓視亞底米為他們的守護神和保護者。在一塊碑銘上，以弗所城稱自己為亞底米的“看守者”，並以此為榮。
**大亞底米。**有文本為“大亞底米女神”。在以弗所的一些碑銘上刻著“最偉大的”，“最高的”。
**從宙斯那裡落下來的像。**Diopetēs，通常指古老史前的神像，例如雅典的雅典娜和特洛伊的帕拉斯（維爾吉《埃涅伊德》第二章第183頁）。該詞也可按字面的意思，指一塊隕石，或直接崇拜，或經過原始的雕刻，因此不一定是指亞底米的神像（見第24節註釋）。根據幾位古代作者說，亞底米的神像不是用石頭做的，而是用金子或橄欖木，黑檀木，雪松木，葡萄木製作的。

18.en: Many that believed came, and confessed. Or, “Many of those who had believed began to come, confessing.” As in v. 2, the verb “believe” is probably used for the whole process of conversion, including baptism (cf. v. 3). These believers had made a profession, but it was clearly an imperfect experience into which they had come. Confessions were now made of wrongdoing, perhaps in some cases in relation to occult practices they had fallen into after they had been baptized. Under the Spirit, the church went through an experience of thorough heart searching. It is not clear whether the confessions were made privately to Paul and the other teachers, or publicly in the presence of the congregation. The latter is the more probable, even as was true of the confessions made to John the Baptist (see on Matt. 3:6). They had seen what the evil one could do with the misuse of the name of Jesus, and wondered whether they were not misusing the name by calling themselves Christians. They realized that they must face Christ as the Judge of all. Their consciences were roused to intense activity. They confessed their sins, thereby coming under the gracious provision of Christ’s forgiveness and intercession (1 John 1:9; 2:1). See AA 288.
18.zh:
那已經信的，多有人來承認訴說自己所行的事。

如本章第2節，“信”可能指悔改的全部過程，包括洗禮（參第3節）。這些信徒曾作過表白，但顯然不完全。他們現在承認錯誤，也許涉及一些他們受洗之後秘密的行為。在聖靈的感動下，教會經歷了一場徹底的自省。不清楚他們是私下到保羅或其他教師面前承認，還是當眾承認。當眾承認的可能性大一些，正像當年人們誠心到施洗約翰那裡認罪一樣（見太3:6註釋）。他們看到惡者如何對付濫用耶穌名字的行為，不知道他們自稱基督徒是否也是濫用了耶穌的名字。他們認識到自己必須面對萬民的審判者耶穌。他們的良心被喚醒積極活動。他們承認自己的罪，因此就來到基督赦免和代求的恩典條件之下（見約壹1:9；2:1）。見《使徒行述》288頁。

25.en: Called. Rather, “gathered.” Demetrius’ craft was the carving and engraving of these shrines, as shown by the word translated “silversmith.” But before the work reached that higher stage, the materials had to pass through many hands in preparation, up to the skilled artisan, who put on the final touches of adornment and polishing. All were concerned in the threatened loss of trade. Sirs. Literally, “men.” By this craft. The word here translated “craft” is the same as that translated “gain” in v. 24, and in both places it may mean “business.” With an almost naive simplicity the words of Demetrius reveal the fact that religion often threatens vested economic interests, and that persecutions may result. This situation greatly increased the difficulties under which Christian evangelists had to labor. Every city had its temples and priests, its oracles and sanctuaries. Sacrifices and feasts created a market for industry that would otherwise have been lacking. Thus in early Christian times, when the gospel was placed in conflict with paganism, the economic interference it presented not infrequently aroused the wrath of those whose incomes were affected.
25.zh:
他聚集他們和同行的工人，說：眾位，你們知道我們是倚靠這生意發財。

**聚集。**底米丟的手藝是雕刻這些神龕，所以被稱為“銀匠”。但產品在達到高級階段之前，材料必須經過許多人的手，再送到熟練的工匠手中，進行最後的裝飾和打磨。所有這些人都擔心行業所面臨的損失。
**眾位。**或“先生們”。
**是倚靠這生意發財。**“生意”與第24節相同。底米丟的話露骨地表明，宗教往往威脅到原有的經濟利益，結果導致逼迫。這種情況大大增加了基督傳道士工作的難度。每一座城市都有廟宇和祭司，廟宇和聖堂。獻祭和節期製造了一個在其他情況下所沒有的市場。所以在基督教的初期，當福音與異教發生衝突的時候，許多情況下都是因為經濟衝突，經濟因素往往引起了收入受影響之人的憤怒。

7.en: Were about twelve. The narrative implies that these 12 formed a group, perhaps attending together the meetings of the church, but not until this time sharing fully in its life.
7.zh:
一共約有十二個人。

暗示這十二個人形成一組，也許一起出席教會的會議，但此前他們並沒有充分參與教會的生活。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第282頁。

2.en: Since ye believed. Or, “having believed.” That is, either when you believed or inasmuch as you believed. Paul addressed the men as believers. Since he had recently arrived, he did not know the background of all who appeared among the members of the congregation. But Paul probably noticed in these men a want of the spiritual gifts, and perhaps a lack of the peace and joy and radiance that were revealed in those brought fully into the message of the gospel. Whether there be any Holy Ghost. The position of these disciples is so like that of Apollos when he arrived at Ephesus that it is reasonable to think they were converts to his preaching. they must, of course, have known the Holy Spirit as a name in the OT and in the teaching of John the Baptist (Matt. 3:11), but beyond that they seemed to be in ignorance concerning the nature of the Spirit. They had received baptism as a token of repentance, and doubtless were leading upright lives, but had not entered upon the experience of “righteousness, and peace, and joy” which was theirs “in the Holy Ghost” (Rom. 14:17). It is evident that they were Jewish and not Gentile disciples.
2.zh:
問他們說：你們信的時候受了聖靈沒有？他們回答說：沒有，也未曾聽見有聖靈賜下來。

**你們信的時候。**或“既然你們信了”。保羅稱他們為信徒。他剛到這裡，不知道會眾中這些人的背景。但保羅可能注意到他們需要屬靈的恩賜，也許缺乏完全接受福音信息的人所表顯的平安，喜樂和光明。
**受了聖靈沒有。**這些門徒的立場與亞波羅到以弗所時的立場相似。我們可以合理地推定，他們信從了亞波羅的道，當然從《舊約》和施洗約翰的教訓中知道聖靈的名字（太3:11），但除此之外，他們對於聖靈的性質似乎一無所知。他們曾領受洗禮，作為悔改的標誌，無疑過正直的生活。但他們還沒有經歷“聖靈中”的“公義，和平，和喜樂”（羅14:17）。他們顯然是猶太人，而不是外邦人。
**懷愛倫註釋（2–3節）**。《使徒行述》第282頁。

10.en: The space of two years. When later he spoke to the Ephesian elders at Miletus, Paul stated that he had admonished the church of Ephesus for “three years” (ch. 20:31). There is no conflict between these two statements. To the two years mentioned here must be added the three months of v. 8 and the time which may have preceded his teaching in the synagogue (see AA 291). All they … in Asia. For “Asia” see on ch. 2:9. Evidently Ephesus became the center of Paul’s labors, and from there he doubtless visited neighboring towns also. Hence there is the possibility that the churches mentioned in Revelation (chs. 2; 3) owe their origin to Paul, though this possibility must be qualified by the statement that some had not seen Paul’s face (Col. 2:1; cf. on Acts 18:23). The growth of the new Christian community in Ephesus, which drew its members from both Jews and Greeks, became a conspicuous fact. The number of gifts to Artemis, and the sale of memorials of her, fell off markedly. Luke implies that the audiences drawn by Paul were made up not only of the settled inhabitants of Ephesus, but of those who visited the city, and who carried news of the preacher and his message to all corners of the district. Philemon from Colossae may have been one of Paul’s converts during this period (see Philemon 19).
10.zh:
這樣有兩年之久，叫一切住在亞西亞的，無論是猶太人，是希利尼人，都聽見主的道。

**這樣有兩年之久。**後來保羅在米利都對以弗所長老講話的時侯，說自己曾勸勉以弗所教會達“三年之久”（徒20:31）。這兩種說法並沒有矛盾。本節所提到的“兩年”必須加上第8節的三個月，以及他在進會堂講道之前可能化掉的時間（見《使徒行述》291頁）。
**一切住在亞細亞的。**關於“亞細亞”，見徒2:9註釋。顯然以弗所成了保羅工作的中心。他無疑從這裡出去訪問周邊的城鎮。所以《啟示錄》所提到的一些教會（啟2；3），有可能是保羅建立的，儘管有人沒有見過他的面（西2:1；參徒18:23）。以弗所基督教新團體的成長，其成員包括猶太人和外邦人，已成為一個顯著的事實。獻給亞底米的禮物減少了。女神紀念品的銷售顯著下降了。路加暗示保羅所吸引的聽眾不僅是以弗所的居民，還有訪問這座城市的人。他們把這位傳道者的新聞和他的信息傳遍這個地區的每一個角落。歌羅西的腓利門可能就是保羅在這段時間勸化的信徒之一（見門19）。

29.en: The whole city. The city was apparently not so much interested in the gains of the silversmiths, as in the glory and magnificence that Ephesus enjoyed as the seat of the worship of Artemis. So the riot, which began in the meeting called by Demetrius, was taken up by the whole Ephesian population. Gaius and Aristarchus. It may be that the crowd sought to find Paul, and not being able to do so, seized these two men. The inclusion of these Macedonian converts in the company of believers gives evidence of the permanent effect of Paul’s labors in that country on his previous journey. The brevity of the record in the Acts makes all the more meaningful these incidental indications, thrown in so undesignedly. “Gaius” represents the Roman name “Caius,” a common Latin name (see Acts 20:4; Rom. 16:23; 1 Cor. 1:14; 3 John 1). Aristarchus was from Thessalonica (Acts 20:4; 27:2), and may already have experienced violence of the sort he now suffered (cf. 1 Thess. 2:14). He appears as one of Paul’s companions in the journey to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4), probably as a delegate from the Macedonian churches. He may have shared the apostle’s imprisonment at Rome (Col. 4:10), either as a fellow prisoner or, more probably, in order to minister to Paul’s needs. Paul’s companions. Just when Gaius and Aristarchus had been “Paul’s companions in travel” is not known. Perhaps they had been the ones who conducted him from Beroea to Athens (ch. 17:15). Possibly their travel with him had been in connection with some unrecorded missionary endeavor outside of Ephesus during the period of his stay there. Into the theatre. That is, doubtless, the amphitheater of Ephesus. Its ruins still remain and give evidence that it could hold 24,500 people. There is no record of anything more being done to Gaius and Aristarchus than their being brought into the theater. Perhaps it was brought that they would reveal Paul’s hiding place. See illustration facing p. 353.
29.zh:
滿城都轟動起來。眾人拿住與保羅同行的馬其頓人該猶和亞裡達古，齊心擁進戲園裡去。

**滿城。**城裡的百姓所關心的，顯然不是銀匠的收入，而是以弗所作為亞底米崇拜中心的榮耀和輝煌。因此底米丟召集會議所發動的暴亂，感染了以弗所全城的人。
**保羅同行的。**不知道該猶和亞里達古何時成為保羅的旅伴。他們也許護送保羅從庇哩亞到雅典（徒17:15），也可能在保羅逗留以弗所期間，曾陪伴他到以弗所以外的地方去，只是沒有記錄下來。
**該猶和亞里達古。**群眾可能想尋找保羅，但沒有找到，於是就抓住這兩個人。信徒的團體中有這些馬其頓人，說明保羅前一次傳道旅程在馬其頓的工作產生了持久的效果。《使徒行傳》簡單的記錄使得這即便是無意的附帶說明也更有意義。“該猶”是一個普通的拉丁名字（見徒20:4；羅16:23；林前1:14；約叄1）。亞里達古來自帖撒羅尼迦（徒20:4；以及徒27:2），可能經歷過他現在遭受的這類暴力（參帖前2:14）。他似乎是保羅去耶路撒冷的一名旅伴（徒20:4），可能是馬其頓教會的代表。他可能與保羅在羅馬一同坐監（西4:10），或許作為獄友，或許為了服侍保羅的需要。
**齊心擁進戲園裡去。**無疑指以弗所的圓形露天劇場。它的廢墟至今依然存在，表明它可以容納24,500人。除了把該猶和亞里達古帶進戲園之外，沒有記錄對他們做了什麼。也許是為了讓他們說出保羅的藏身之處。見本卷註釋第353頁的說明。

26.en: Ye see and hear. The silversmith reminds them that they are eyewitnesses of what is taking place at Ephesus—the falling off in demand for the products surrounding the worship, as the preaching and preachers of Christianity spread far and wide. Throughout all Asia. The speech of Demetrius, though doubtless colored by his own fears, confirms the statement of v. 10 concerning the success of Paul’s labors. As has already been noted, it is possible that Paul’s writings, if not his presence, reached Colossae, Laodicea, and Hierapolis. Churches in the nearby cities of Pergamus, Smyrna, Thyatira, Sardis, and Philadelphia are mentioned in the Revelation. In one way or another the gospel had spread widely throughout the region now called Asia Minor. Pliny, in his epistle to Trajan (Letters x. 96), nearly half a century later, uses language similar to that of Demetrius. He speaks of temples “almost deserted” and “but few purchasers” for sacrificial victims, in the region of Pontus just to the northeast of Ephesus. This Paul. If the bodily presence of Paul was truly as unimpressive as he himself described it (see 2 Cor. 10:10; Gal. 4:13–15), we can easily imagine the scorn Demetrius threw into the words as he referred to “this Paul.” Turned away much people. They were turned away from their devotion to Artemis, and so from the purchase of the shrines and other materials on sale in connection with the temple. They be no gods. See on Acts 14:14, 15; 1 Cor. 8:4. In anger, Demetrius virtually committed himself to the opposite idea—that the idol was a god. Pagan philosophers always insisted that the images were merely symbolic and ideal representations.
26.zh:
這保羅不但在以弗所，也幾乎在亞西亞全地，引誘迷惑許多人，說：人手所做的，不是神。這是你們所看見所聽見的。

**這保羅。**如果保羅的體貌真的像他自己所說的那麼不出眾的話（見林後10:10；加4:13-15），我們就很容易想像底米丟所說“這保羅”的諷刺意味了。
**在亞細亞全地。**底米丟的話無疑添加了自己的恐懼，但證實了第10節關於保羅工作成功的話。如上所述，即使保羅沒有親自去，他的書信也已傳到歌羅西、老底嘉和希拉波立。《啟示錄》提到了附近的城市別迦摩，士每拿，推雅推喇，撒狄和非拉鐵非。福音以各種途徑傳遍了現在被稱為小亞細亞的地區。大約半個世紀之後，普林尼用與底米丟相似的話寫信給圖拉真說（《書信》第十章第96頁），在以弗所東北的本都地區，廟宇“幾乎全都荒廢”，祭品的“購買者寥寥無幾”。
**引誘迷惑許多人。**他們不再崇拜亞底米，所以不再購買神龕和其他與神廟有關的物品。
**人手所作的，不是神。**見徒14:14,15；林前8:4註釋。事實上底米丟在盛怒之下承認了相反的觀點──偶像是神。異教哲學家們總是堅持認為，偶像只是象徵和理想的表達。
**你們所看見所聽見的。**這位銀匠提醒說，他們都是以弗所發生之事的目擊證人。由於基督教的傳播和傳道士活動範圍的不斷擴大，與偶像崇拜相關的產品需求量減少了。

24.en: Demetrius. This man is not otherwise known. The name was common among the Greeks. Shrines. Gr. naoi (singular, naos; see on Matt. 4:5). This word, commonly translated “temple” always refers to the inner sanctuary, where the divine presence was supposed to dwell, and here must, accordingly, mean the inner sanctuary containing the statue of the goddess. The small silver (or terra-cotta) representations of the temple probably contained a tiny statue of the goddess. These models could either be placed in a house or worn as a charm. Diana. Gr. Artemis. There seems to have been no good reason for the KJV translators to use here the name of the Roman goddess Diana, who was identified only approximately with the Ephesian deity, instead of the name that appears in the Greek text. From early times the worship of Artemis, originally an Asiatic cult, had centered at Ephesus. When the Greeks sent colonies to Asia Minor they found this form of religion already established there, and, from some resemblance that they discovered in the worship, they gave to the Asian divinity the name of the Greek goddess Artemis. The fourth temple to Artemis owed much of its magnificence to Croesus. It is said to have been burned down on the night of the birth of Alexander the Great in 356 B.C., by Herostratus, who was impelled by an insane desire to secure an immortality of renown, or rather notoriety, by this act. In the time of Alexander the Great the temple was rebuilt, more stately than ever, and came to be considered one of the Seven Wonders of the World. Its porticoes were adorned with paintings and sculptures by the great masters of Greek art. It had its coterie of priests, priestesses, and boy attendants. Children employed in the temple services were given an education, and priests and priestesses were pensioned after the age of 60 (cf. 1 Tim. 5:9). One class of priests, known as the theologoi, were assigned to interpret the mysteries of the cult. Large contributions were made toward the support of the temple, whose benefactors were accorded the highest honors the city could bestow. Pilgrims from all parts of the world came to worship, and purchased memorials made of silver, bronze, marble, or clay. These represented the sanctuary, and the image of Diana that was within. The upper part of the image of Diana was that of a female figure with many breasts. From the waist down it was simply a square column ornamented with mysterious symbols, including bees, ears of corn, and flowers strangely intermingled. It had been carved in wood, and was now black with age. There is a reproduction of this figure in the Vatican Museum, which seems more like that of some strange Oriental idol. Perhaps its very ugliness was the secret of its presumed power. The first real blow that idolatry had received in Ephesus for centuries was that dealt by Paul during his residence in the city. Strangely enough, the next came from the hand of the insane Nero, who robbed the temple of Artemis as he had robbed others in Greece and Asia (Tacitus Annals xv. 45), in order to adorn his Golden House at Rome with their treasures of art. Trajan later sent its richly sculptured gates as a gift to a temple at Byzantium, the site of the later city of Constantinople. As Christianity advanced the worship of Artemis naturally declined, and ere long her shrines were largely deserted. When the Goths devastated Asia Minor about A.D. 262 they plundered the temple of Diana, and its destruction was completed centuries later by the Turks. When the empire became Christian, the temple of Ephesus, in common with that of Delphi, supplied materials for the church of St. Sophia, erected by Justinian in Constantinople in honor of the Holy Wisdom. Since the Turkish invasion the church has served as a mosque. It is now a museum. The city of Ephesus fell into such a state of decay that the site of the temple was uncertain until within the last century. Excavations have since revealed the temple site and have brought to light many inscriptions connected with it. Gain. Gr. ergasia, “work,” “business”; also “gain produced from works,” that is, profit. The word is used twice in ch. 16:16, 19, of the “gain” made by the Philippian masters from the ravings of the girl who was possessed. The craftsmen at Ephesus created the uproar because their profits were disappearing. Perhaps Demetrius himself, the fiercest of all the rioters, did none of the actual work, but through employing many workmen received a large share of the gains. All the imagery and symbolism of Artemis would furnish an abundant opportunity for the craft of the silversmiths.
24.zh:
有一個銀匠，名叫底米丟，是製造亞底米神銀龕的，他使這樣手藝人生意發達。

**底米丟。**其他地方沒有提到這個人。這個名字在希臘人中很普遍。
**亞底米。**Artemis。有文本為“羅馬黛安娜女神”。自古以來，源於亞細亞宗教的亞底米崇拜，就是以以弗所為中心的。當希臘人在亞細亞建立殖民地的時候，發現那裡已經建立了這種宗教，以及與他們自己信仰的一些雷同之處，於是就給這個亞細亞神明起了希臘女神亞底米的名字。
亞底米第四個廟宇的富麗堂皇，主要靠的是克羅伊斯。據說在公元前356年亞歷山大大帝出生的那天夜晚，這座廟宇被西羅司達斯燒燬。西羅司達斯被一種瘋狂的慾望所驅使，希望自己的名聲永垂不朽，或遺臭萬年。在亞歷山大大帝的時候，廟宇得到重建，比以前更加氣派，被稱為世界七大奇觀之一。廟宇的柱廊是由希臘著名藝術大師的繪畫和雕刻裝飾的。廟宇中有專職的祭司和女祭司，還有一些男孩作為侍者。受僱於神廟崇事的孩子，在那裡接受教育。祭司以及女祭司在60歲之後可以領到養老金（參提前5:9）。有一班祭司被稱為theologoi，被指定解釋宗教中的奧秘。
有大量的捐款維持著這座神廟。捐助人被授予這座城市的最高榮譽。世界各地的香客前來朝拜，併購買用銀子、銅、大理石或者陶土製作的紀念品。這些紀念品代表殿宇，裡面有亞底米的神像。
亞底米神像的上半部分是具有多個乳房的女性形象。腰部以下只是一個方形柱體，上面裝飾著神秘的符號，包括混合奇異的蜜蜂，玉米穗和鮮花。神像是木雕的，現因為年代久遠而發黑。梵蒂岡博物館有這個雕像的複製品，看上去更像東方的古怪偶像。也許它的醜陋是人們假象它能力的秘密所在。
多世紀以來，這種偶像崇拜在以弗所遭到的第一次真正打擊是保羅住在這座城市期間引起的。奇怪的是，下一次打擊卻是來自瘋狂的尼祿。他搶劫了希臘和亞細亞的其他神廟，也搶劫了亞底米女神的廟宇（塔西圖《編年史》第十五章第45頁），為了用這些藝術珍寶裝飾自己在羅馬城的金屋。圖拉真後來把這座廟宇精心雕刻的大門作為禮物送給拜佔廷的一個神廟。拜佔廷就是後來的君士坦丁堡。
由於基督教的發展，亞底米的崇拜自然衰落了。不久之後，她的神龕就少有人問津。公元262年哥特人蹂躪小亞細亞的時候，洗劫了亞底米神廟。幾個世紀之後，土耳其人徹底摧毀了這個神廟。當羅馬帝國成為了基督徒國家時，以弗所的神廟和特爾斐的神廟一樣，為聖索非亞教堂提供材料。這個教堂是查士丁尼在君士坦丁堡為尊崇神聖智慧而建造的。土耳其人入侵之後，它變成了一座清真寺。現為博物館。以弗所淪為廢墟，直到十九世紀才找到廟宇的遺址，發掘出許多相關的碑銘。
**龕。**naoi（單數naos，見太4:5註釋）。一般譯為“殿宇”，通常指內殿，據認為有神臨格，因此本節應該指奉有女神神像的內殿。小型的銀製（或陶土製）神龕裡面可能有一尊微型的女神像。這些模型既可擺在家裡，也可戴在身上作為裝飾。
**生意。**ergasia，“工作”，“業務”以及“產品的收益”，即利潤。該詞在徒16:16,19出現兩次，指腓立比的主人們藉著被鬼附身的使女所獲得的“財利”。以弗所的工匠發起了這場動亂，因為他們的利潤越來越少。也許鬧事的人中最瘋狂的底米丟本人並沒有做什麼實際的工作，而是藉著僱傭許多工人獲去大額利潤。亞底米的一切肖像和象徵物為銀匠的手藝提供了大量的機會。

8.en: Into the synagogue. In keeping with apostolic custom (see on ch. 9:20). These visitations were doubtless mainly on the Sabbath days, in the first place because Paul was a Sabbathkeeper (see chs. 13:14; 16:13), and also because Paul labored with his hands during the week (Acts 18:3; 20:34; 1 Thess. 2:9; 2 Thess. 3:8), and because Sabbaths presented the best opportunities for establishing contact with the Jews. Spake boldly. See on ch. 9:27 Space of three months. These brief words cover the record of a period of heavy labor. Doubtless daily work as a tentmaker went on for Paul as before (cf. ch. 20:34), while on the Sabbaths at least he was in the synagogue preaching that Jesus is the Christ, and setting forth the nature of His work and the eternal laws of His kingdom. Disputing. Rather, “reasoning,” as in chs. 17:2; 18:4, 19; see on ch. 20:7. Persuading. Or, “attempting to persuade.” Kingdom of God. See on ch. 1:6.
8.zh:
保羅進會堂，放膽講道，一連三個月，辯論神國的事，勸化眾人。

**進會堂。**這符合使徒的習慣（見徒9:20註釋）。進入會堂無疑主要在安息日，首先因為保羅是遵守安息日的人（見徒13:14；16:13），也因為保羅在平日要用雙手勞動（徒18:3；20:34；見帖前2:9；帖後3:8），並因為安息日提供了與猶太人接觸的最好機會。
**放膽講道。**見徒9:27註釋。
**一連三個月。**這幾個字記錄了一段勞碌的時期。保羅無疑像以前一樣每天從事帳篷的製作（參徒20:34），但至少在安息日，他在會堂裡傳耶穌是基督，並教導祂工作的性質和祂國度的永恆律法。
**辯論。**或“探討”如徒17:2；18:4,19；見徒20:7註釋。
**上帝國。**見徒1:6註釋。
**勸化。**或“試圖說服”。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–9節）**。《使徒行述》第285頁。

23.en: No small stir. A negative understatement for emphasis. About that way. Literally, “the way,” but the Greek article often has demonstrative force. See on ch. 9:2.
23.zh:
那時，因為這道起的擾亂不小。

**因為這道。**見徒9:2註釋。
**起的擾亂不小。**一種否定的含蓄陳述，為了強調。
**懷愛倫註釋（23–27節）**。《使徒行述》第292頁。

27.en: Craft. Gr. meros, “part,” “portion,” that is, branch, of business. Meros is not the Greek word translated “craft” in v. 25. Great goddess. The adjective “great” (megas) was especially used of Artemis of Ephesus. It appears on many of the coins and medals of the city. Should be despised. Literally, “may be counted for nothing.” This would be the case if men began to think that the gods represented by the work of men’s hands were not truly gods. In his eagerness, Demetrius forgot to put forward what the town clerk mentioned afterward (v. 35), that the image was supposed to have come down from heaven. He was interested only in the matter of the income in connection with the worship of the goddess. The silversmith of Ephesus had become unconsciously a prophet of future doom for paganism. Her magnificence … destroyed. Rather, “to be about to be cast down from her greatness.” The great goddess was on the point of being robbed of her greatness. The Greek word rendered “magnificence” is not infrequently used to express the majesty of God. All Asia and the world. Asia was one of the proconsular provinces, and the word “world” is used conventionally, as in Luke 2:1, for the Roman Empire. Wealth from the East as well as from Greece, and even from the people of Rome, was bestowed on this gorgeous shrine.
27.zh:
這樣，不獨我們這事業被人藐視，就是大女神亞底米的廟也要被人輕忽，連亞西亞全地和普天下所敬拜的大女神之威榮也要消滅了。

**事業。**meros，“部分”，指行業，與第25節中的“生意”原文不是同一個詞。
**大女神。**形容詞“大”（megas）特指以弗所的亞底米。它出現在以弗所的許多硬幣和獎章上。
**要被人輕忽。**直譯為“被人視為虛無”。如果人開始認識到人手所造的物品並不是真正的神明，情況就會是這樣。底米丟情急之下忘記提出以弗所城書記後來提到的事（第35節）：神像被認為是從天上掉下來的。他只關心與女神崇拜有關的收入問題。以弗所的這個銀匠不知不覺預言了異教的厄運。
**亞細亞全地和普天下。**亞細亞是地方總督所管轄的行省。這裡的“普天下”如路2:1一樣，通常指羅馬帝國。來自希臘，東方，甚至羅馬百姓的財富，都花在這座華麗的神廟上。
**大女神之威榮…要消滅了。**大女神的威榮將被剝奪。希臘語的“威榮”常用來表示上帝的最威嚴。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第295頁。

34.en: Knew. Or, “perceived.” The man’s Jewish features and dress only seemed to arouse the mob further, knowing as they did the Jewish abhorrence of idolatry. Jews were accused of trafficking in goods stolen from the temples (see on Rom. 2:22). The language of the town clerk (Acts 19:37) suggests the same thought, for he could point to Aristarchus and Gaius and declare emphatically, “These men are not temple robbers.” All with one voice. The mob now had one object upon which to focus their uproar, and for two hours they kept repeating the cry. It is evident from this that the Jews were not popular; the wrath aroused against the Jew, Paul, by Demetrius’ speech was now about to be turned against the whole body of Jews in the city.
34.zh:
只因他們認出他是猶太人，就大家同聲喊著說：大哉！以弗所人的亞底米啊。如此約有兩小時。

**認出。**亞歷山大猶太人的特徵和著裝更加激怒了暴徒。他們知道猶太人恨惡偶像崇拜。有人指控猶太人經銷廟中偷來之物（見羅2:22註釋）。以弗所城書記的話（徒19:37）表達了同樣的意思，因為他指著亞里達古和該猶強調說：“這些人沒有偷竊廟中之物”。
**大家同聲喊著說。**暴徒們現在只有一個騷亂的目的。他們喊叫了兩個小時。由此可見，他們不歡迎猶太人。底米丟的演講所煽動對一個猶太人保羅的怒氣，如今要轉到全城所有的猶太人身上了。

32.en: Cried. Or, “kept on crying.” The vividness of the narrative marks it as being an eyewitness account. Aristarchus and Gaius, companions of Paul en route to Jerusalem (ch. 20:4), may have related the story to Luke. Assembly. Gr. ekklēsia, a group “called out.” The mob that had gathered in the amphitheater was not an ekklēsia, in the sense of a legal, governmental assembly, such as the word implied in classical usage (see on Matt. 18:17; cf. on Acts 19:39). Rather the word is used here in a looser sense for an unorganized crowd. Confused. Literally, “poured together,” “mixed [violently].” An unthinking mob blindly follows its leaders. Knew not wherefore. Were it not so tragic, in that the success of the gospel was at stake, Luke’s description of a large crowd shouting and milling around in the amphitheater, the majority not even knowing for sure why they were there, would be ludicrous.
32.zh:
聚集的人紛紛亂亂，有喊叫這個的，有喊叫那個的，大半不知道是為什麼聚集。

**聚集的人。**ekklēsia，集會。暴徒聚集在戲園裡，並不是舉行合法的政治集會，如ekklēsia在古典時期所表達的（見太18:17註釋；參徒19:39註釋）。更確切地講，這是指一群烏合之眾。
**紛紛亂亂。**直譯為“混合在一起”。一群沒有頭腦的暴徒盲目地跟隨他們的首領。
**喊叫。**或“不住地喊叫”。生動的描寫表明來自目擊證人。陪伴保羅到耶路撒冷的亞里達古和該猶（徒20:4），可能把這個故事告訴路加。
**不知道為什麼。**假如不是一場悲劇，因為福音的勝利處在危急關頭，路加所描述大批群眾在戲園裡狂呼亂叫，多數人甚至不知道自己為什麼來的狀況，真是荒唐可笑。
**懷愛倫註釋（32–41節）**。《使徒行述》第294頁。

11.zh:
神藉保羅的手行了些非常的奇事；

**藉保羅的手。**源於希伯來習語，意為“假借”（見徒5:12註釋）。
**行了。**原文動詞的時態暗示保羅在以弗所期間，上帝能力的不斷彰顯。不是指因某一次大有能力的講道所導致的偶然彰顯。
**非常的奇事。**直譯是“大能的（作為），不是偶然發生的”，不是任何日子都有的（參徒28:2註釋）。“奇事”的希臘語是“dunamis”（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷五第208頁）。上帝施行奇事。保羅只是工具。
**懷愛倫註釋（11–12節）**。《使徒行述》第286頁；【 SDA6.1064】。

12.zh:
甚至有人從保羅身上拿手巾或圍裙放在病人身上，病就退了，惡鬼也出去了。

**從保羅的身上拿手巾或圍裙。**希臘語的“手巾”和“圍裙”譯自拉丁語。“手巾”（希臘語sudaria）用來擦臉上的汗水；“圍裙”（希臘語semicinctia）是工匠穿戴短圍裙。奇怪的是，路加用簡單幾筆帶過兩年的傳道工作之後，竟敘述了這些細節。出於他作醫生的興趣，他自然會關注超自然的治療現象。保羅在從事手藝的時候，似乎有一些誠心前來的人，得到了保羅所用的手巾和圍裙。這些物件的治療效果，相當於耶穌衣裳的貼邊（見可5:27,28註釋）和祂用來醫治瞎子的泥（見約9:6註釋）。上帝超自然的醫治，有兩個普遍適用的條件：神能和信心。聯接神能與人信心的物質，只是運用信心的工具。
**病就退了。**如本章所示，在以弗所城裡，巫術和符咒的法術和怪異的技巧，都在百姓眼前炫耀。上帝似乎以神奇的治療，作為信心能力的特殊證據。

13.zh:
那時，有幾個遊行各處、唸咒趕鬼的猶太人，向那被惡鬼附的人擅自稱主耶穌的名，說：我奉保羅所傳的耶穌勒令你們出來！

**遊行各處、唸咒趕鬼的猶太人。**或“遊行各處的猶太驅魔師”。騙子們試圖用保羅和耶穌的名字牟利。這些猶太人自稱能用魔法和符咒治病（見徒8:9；13:6註釋）。猶太人的歷史學家約瑟夫斯在寫到據傳的所羅門驅魔趕鬼的技術時補充說：“這種療法至今在我們中間都大有能力”（見《猶太古代史》第八章2.5 [46]；洛伯版，第五冊第595頁）。
**向…擅自稱主耶穌的名。**從很早的時候起，猶太傳統文學就把偉大的成果歸因於奉無法表達的上帝之名。他們說摩西就是藉此殺死埃及人的。以利沙也是“奉耶和華的名”消滅嘲笑的孩子的。我們不難理解這些“遊行各處” 猶太人看到了保羅奉耶穌之名的效果，就試圖用同一個名去醫病（參徒3:16）。
**我奉。**有文本為“我們奉”。“我奉”無疑是對的，因為驅魔時說話的是一個人。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–16節）**。《使徒行述》第287頁。

14.zh:
做這事的，有猶太祭司長士基瓦的七個兒子。

**做這事的。**士基瓦的七個兒子用以上的話驅魔。這句套話似乎給他們帶來了尊敬。
**猶太祭司長。**或“一位猶太祭司長”。暗示他是24班祭司中一班的首領（見太2:4；路3:2註釋）。若是這樣，這個人可能因某種原因已失去了職務，但到以弗所之後，依然自稱為祭司長。路加也這樣稱呼他。

15.zh:
惡鬼回答他們說：耶穌我認識，保羅我也知道。你們卻是誰呢？

**惡鬼回答他們說。**驅魔師與惡鬼面面相對。惡鬼與當年在加大拉與主相遇時一樣強悍兇暴（可5:3,4；參太8:28）。
**耶穌我認識。**ton Iēsoun ginōskō。“Ginōskō”不僅暗示親自認識，而且承認權威。
**保羅我也知道。**ton Paulon epistamai。Epistamai可能暗示熟悉或瞭解。
你們卻是誰呢？被鬼附著的人就這樣與惡鬼合為一體（參可5:7-12）。他害怕保羅這樣的人提說耶穌之名，但不怕這些騙子提說。

16.zh:
惡鬼所附的人就跳在他們身上，勝了其中二人，制伏他們，叫他們赤著身子受了傷，從那房子裡逃出去了。

**跳在他們身上。**惡鬼附身，就像加大拉人的例子一樣，給了受害者異常的力氣。他發作的時候，騙子驚慌逃竄了。
**勝了其中二人。**有文本為“勝了他們”。可能指七個兒子中只有兩個捲入此事。然而蒲紙文獻證明原文的“二 ”也可指“所有”的，不止兩人。
**赤著身子。**不一定指扯掉了外套，只剩下短上衣（見太5:40註釋）。記錄到此結束。如果作者是在編造離奇的事情，他就可能把故事講高潮，說士基瓦的兒子們失敗之後，患者在保羅的手中得了醫治。但路加的記錄是以事實為依據的。

17.zh:
凡住在以弗所的，無論是猶太人，是希利尼人，都知道這事，也都懼怕；主耶穌的名從此就尊大了。

**都知道這事。**這個故事無疑很快傳遍了當地。士基瓦的兒子們對這件事可能沒什麼說的。
**主耶穌的名從此就尊大了。**動詞的時態暗示持續的尊崇。這裡的敘述表明耶穌的名遠高過那些趕鬼的人所用的任何其他名字，同時顯明如果不憑著信心貿然使用這個名字是很危險的。當以弗所的百姓看見褻瀆這名的人所遭受的懲罰時，他們就空前地尊敬這名。
**懷愛倫註釋（17–20節）**。《使徒行述》第288頁；《給青年人的信息》第275-278頁。

20.zh:
主的道大大興旺，而且得勝，就是這樣。

**主的道大大興旺。**“大大”可以理解為“具有壓倒一切，無法抗拒的力量”。
**而且得勝。**或“繼續增強”。

21.zh:
這些事完了，保羅心裡定意經過了馬其頓、亞該亞，就往耶路撒冷去；又說：我到了那裡以後，也必須往羅馬去看看。

**這些事完了。**在以弗所有許多人加入教會。上帝藉著引人注目的事件，參與了教會和城市的活動。“信”的人經歷了一場變革。邪惡的工具毀滅了，十分壯觀，吸引了全城的注意。工作奠定了良好的基礎。保羅覺得可以離開這座城市了。
**心裡定意。**原文意義含糊；可以指保羅自己的心意，也可以指保羅在聖靈的感動下拿定主意（見徒17:16註釋）。
**經過了馬其頓、亞該亞。**《哥林多前書》提供了保羅意圖的背景。保羅在以弗所年間，多少與馬其頓和亞該亞的教會有所接觸，因此有牽掛的理由。他必須給哥林多教會寫一封信，但是這封信沒有保留下來，信中警告他們防備淫亂的大罪（林前5:9-11）。革來氏家裡的人帶來了結黨紛爭的消息；保羅還聽到教會嚴重混亂，缺乏紀律，甚至出現亂倫的罪（林前1:115:1；11:18-22）。這些事情需要保羅親自關注。保羅還希望能再次訪問耶路撒冷，並且將外邦教會的捐款帶給巴勒斯坦貧窮的猶太籍基督徒（見林前16:1；林後8:1-4）。
**往耶路撒冷去。**為攜帶上述的捐款。保羅曾說到“在以弗所同野獸戰鬥”（林前15:32），和在以弗所有“寬大又有功效的門”為他“開了”（林前16:9）。保羅在以弗所經歷的嚴重困難，對於他來說既是機會的門，也是嚴重的威脅。現在他可以離開了，去訪問希臘的教會，然後去耶路撒冷。
**往羅馬去看看。**這是第一次記錄保羅希望到羅馬去。保羅打算去羅馬（見羅1:13；15:23）表明這是他多年的宿願，可能是在他最處蒙召做外邦人的使徒時就有的（徒22:21）。他在羅馬有許多朋友，這無疑加強了他去帝國首都的願望。這些朋友是他在其他地方認識的（羅16:1-15）。保羅覺得，他如果不能到帝國的偉大中心作見證，他的工作就不完全。但這些希望他一直沒有實現；因此在他離開以弗所的時候，他宣佈自己定意去羅馬以及西班牙（羅15:28）。
**懷愛倫註釋（21–22節）**。《使徒行述》第291頁。

22.zh:
於是從幫助他的人中打發提摩太、以拉都二人往馬其頓去，自己暫時等在亞西亞。

**幫助。**“diakoneō”（“服務”）。名詞“執事”源於這個動詞。參本卷註釋第25頁。
**提摩太。**關於提摩太的使命，見林前4:17。他先被派去警戒勸勉信徒，為使保羅去訪問哥林多的時候不至於過度勞累。保羅勸勉哥林多信徒恭敬地接納提摩太（林前16:10）。後來他奉命回到保羅那裡（同上第11節），因此在保羅寫《哥林多後書》時，他同使徒在一起（林後1:1）。
**以拉都。**在哥林多曾經發現一塊鋪路石，可以追溯到公元一世紀中期，上面刻著：“為報答市政官，以拉都自己出資鋪路”。學者們普遍認為他就是本節所提到的以拉都（見羅16:23註釋；參提後4:20）。
**往馬其頓去。**無疑為了讓各教會的捐款預備好，而且正如他寫給哥林多信徒樣，不必等他到時再現湊（林前16:2）。

36.zh:
這事既是駁不倒的，你們就當安靜，不可造次。

**駁。**城裡的書記宣稱沒有人能反駁他的話。他的話更象關於既定宗教的官方聲明，而不象表達個人對宗教的虔誠。
**就當安靜。**或“有秩序”。該詞的另一種形式在本章的35節譯成 “安撫”。
**不可造次。**直譯是“不可貿然行事”。這個形容詞充分表達了沒有理由，沒有好處，固執蠻橫的喧囂，以及群眾捉拿那兩個沒有犯罪，無法訴訟之人的鹵莽行為。

37.zh:
你們把這些人帶來，他們並沒有偷竊廟中之物，也沒有謗讟我們的女神。

**偷竊廟中之物。**由於以弗所壯麗的神廟裡有一個龐大的庫房，這種罪行不會不為人知。廟中的一切物品都受女神保護，故現為神廟的財產。偷竊神廟中的任何物品都算是褻瀆。見第34節註釋。
**我們的女神。**有文本為“你們的女神”。根據流行的稱謂，說話的人自然將自己與市民同胞視為一體。從本節我們可以理解，保羅和他的同伴在提到以弗所的特殊崇拜時，語言十分謹慎。他們倡導一個偉大的原則，即人手所製作的不是神，並讓這句話產生效果（第26節）。在雅典的時候，儘管保羅“看見滿城都是偶像”心裡著急（徒17:16），他依然保持這份剋制。

38.zh:
若是底米丟和他同行的人有控告人的事，自有放告的日子（或作：自有公堂），也有方伯可以彼此對告。

**有…事。**指如果有具體的控告，就提出來。如果事情真像他們所說的那樣，那就可以作為訴訟的依據。但銅匠和他的朋友們製造騷亂是沒有理由的。
**自有放告的日子（或作“自有公堂”）。**譯文表達了大概的意思。原文是複數，指規定聽訟的時間。或根據動詞的時態指現在有訴訟的機會：“法院正在開庭”。
**方伯。**anthupatoi（參徒13:7,8,12；18:12）。亞細亞是由地方總督治理的行省（見徒6:9註釋）。本節難解之處是“方伯”用了複數，因為一個省同時只能有一個方伯。因此以弗所書記所說的，只能是一位方伯。有以下幾種解釋：（1）指方伯的助理（consiliarii）。（2）書記可能提醒百姓帝國憲法關於伸張冤情的規定，似乎是說： “方伯是帝國設立的。在每一個像我們那樣的省份，都有一個這樣的最高長官，因此不要擔心真正的傷害不會得到補償”。（3）方伯錫拉努斯最近遭到拘禁（參塔西圖《編年史》第十三章第1頁）。這個複數的“方伯”可能指負責帝國在亞細亞事務的西勒和赫留斯。（4）可能基利家，塞浦路斯，庇推尼等鄰近省份的另一位方伯此時在以弗所。在上述四種解釋中，第二種似乎比較合理。
**對告。**egkaleō，“指控”，“訴訟”。底米丟和他的追隨者應該正式起訴被告。被告可以提出反駁，雙方進行辯論，各自出具證據。

39.zh:
你們若問別的事，就可以照常例聚集斷定。

**你們若問。**或“如果你們尋求什麼事情”。
**別的事情。**顯然有些事情可以呈到方伯那裡審判，其他事情則可以在會上解決。
**照常例聚集。**根據傳統，希臘城市要舉行公眾集會，處理公共事務。城裡的書記暗示，他面前的暴徒並不是舉行合法的集會。根據克里索斯說（《聖經佈道》第四十二章，徒19:21,23註釋），合法的集會每月有三次。

40.zh:
今日的擾亂本是無緣無故，我們難免被查問。論到這樣聚眾，我們也說不出所以然來。

**今日的擾亂。**或“今天的暴亂”。
**被查問。**或“控告”。
**聚眾。**sustrophē，“扭在一起”，“密謀”，“混亂”。

41.zh:
說了這話，便叫眾人散去。

他有這樣做的權力。可能他最後的話對聽眾起了很大的作用。如果他們的這種暴行傳到羅馬，他們城市的特權就會受到削弱。城裡的書記安撫了暴徒，吩咐他們散去，安靜地回家。

27.en: The church. That is, the Christian congregation at Antioch, which had been moved by the Spirit (ch. 13:2) to send them on their journey. It was fitting that the apostles should report to this church the results of their First Missionary Journey. Rehearsed all. During the interval of the missionary tour the Christians had probably heard little or nothing from the apostles, and we may well picture the eagerness with which they now gathered to listen to the report. God had done. The great things they had accomplished were actually the acts of God. Opened the door. This meaningful phrase is a favorite metaphor of Paul (see 1 Cor. 16:9; 2 Cor. 2:12; Col. 4:3), and occurs here probably as a fragment from his speech. Unto the Gentiles. The gospel privileges had been given to everyone who believed. This freedom was first offered to the Gentiles at Antioch, where Paul had assisted Barnabas and others in the work (ch. 11:20–26). The gospel had now been carried to the Gentiles over a much wider field. Paul was fulfilling his commission to go to the Gentiles (ch. 22:21).
27.zh:
到了那裡，聚集了會眾，就述說神藉他們所行的一切事，並神怎樣為外邦人開了信道的門。

**會眾。**指安提阿的基督徒會眾。他們曾受聖靈感動（徒13:2），差遣保羅和巴拿巴外出。如今使徒們回來向這個教會彙報他們第一次傳道旅程的成果是很合適的。
**述說…一切事。**使徒們外出傳道期間，基督徒可能很少聽到、甚至沒有聽到他們的消息。我們可以想象信徒當時聚集要聽彙報的迫切心情。
**上帝…所行。**他們所行的大事，事實上是上帝的作為。
**開了信道的門。**這是保羅最喜愛用的比喻（見林前16:9；林後2:12；西4:3），出現在這裡可能是他講論的一部分。
**為外邦人。**福音的特權賜給每一個相信的人。這種自由首先提供給安提阿的外邦人。在那裡保羅幫助巴拿巴和其他人工作（徒11:20-26）。福音現在已經在大得多的領域裡傳給了外邦人。保羅正在履行他在對邦人的使命（徒22:21）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第188頁。

23.en: Ordained. Gr. cheirotoneō, literally, “to extend the hand.” This word was used among the Greeks for the action of electing officials by show of hands; from this was derived the general meaning, “to elect,” without particular regard to the method employed (see 2 Cor. 8:19, where cheirotoneō is translated, “chosen”); and from this was developed the further meaning, “to appoint,” whether by election or by other means (see Acts 10:41). On the basis of this verb some scholars have suggested that the elders chosen at Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch were elected by popular vote. Although it is probably true that some system of election was practiced in the apostolic church (see Acts 6:3; 2 Cor. 8:19), serious doubt must be entertained as to whether such was the method of selection employed here. The present passage indicates that Paul and Barnabas, rather than the churches, made the selection, and in view of this, the broader meaning of “chose,” or “appointed,” appears to be the best translation. Though formal ordination doubtless took place (see 1 Tim. 4:14; 5:22; 2 Tim. 1:6), it is not necessarily implied by the verb used here. Local circumstances probably were such that the apostles felt it was wiser to appoint officers directly in these new churches than to open the matter to a general election. Paul seems to have recommended a similar procedure to Titus (Titus 1:5). At a later time bishops were elected regularly by vote of the clergy and the people. Thus Fabian of Rome was chosen by the people in A.D. 236 (Eusebius Ecclesiastical History vi. 29. 2–4). Cyprian of Carthage (d. A.D. 258) speaks of the “suffrage of the whole brotherhood” (Epistle lxvii. 5; ANF, vol. 5, p. 371). The Constitutions of the Holy Apostles (probably 4th century) provide that the church leaders are to be “chosen by the whole people” (viii. 2. 4; ANF, vol. 7, p. 481). From the 4th century on it was the established policy for a new bishop to be nominated by neighboring bishops, and his name approved by the clergy and laity of his diocese. In the Middle Ages the laity meant, of course, the aristocracy, not the common man. Elders. See on ch. 11:30. By virtue of the authority vested in them as missionaries (see ch. 13:3), Paul and Barnabas led out in the choice of elders. Thus they instituted in the Gentile churches a form of organization already adopted by Christians in Jerusalem. It was based on the synagogue rather than on the Temple (see Vol. V, p. 57). Paul organized these churches soon after their members had become Christians, which fact shows that organization is essential for maintaining the spiritual life and growth of the church. Prayed with fasting. As had been the procedure when the apostles themselves were sent forth from Antioch (see on ch. 13:3). Commended. That is, “committed.” This word suggests the confidence one person feels in another to whom he has committed the keeping of his treasured possessions. In the present case it implies absolute trust in God.
23.zh:
二人在各教會中選立了長老，又禁食禱告，就把他們交託所信的主。

**選立了。**“cheirotoneō,”，直譯是“伸手”。該詞在希臘人中表示舉手示意選舉官員，故引申為泛指“選舉”，而不是特指選舉的方式（見林後8:19，cheirotoneō譯為“挑選”）；又據此進一步引申為用選舉或其他方法“委任”（見徒10:41）。根據這個動詞，一些學者認為路司得，以哥念和安提阿的長老是通過普選產生的。儘管在使徒時代的教會可能實行了某種選舉的制度（見徒6:3；林後8:19），但這裡是否使用了這種制度，尚存在很大的疑問。本節說明是保羅和巴拿巴，而不是教會進行選立，有鑑於此，廣義的“選”和“立”似乎是最好的譯文。儘管正式的按立無疑已經發生（見提前4:14；5:22；提後1:6），這裡的動詞不一定暗示這個意思。當地的環境可能讓使徒們覺得在這些新建立的教會中直接任命職員要比普選更為明智。保羅似乎曾向提多推薦這樣的程序（多1:5）。
後來，主教由和神職人員和信徒定期選舉產生。羅馬的費邊就是這樣由信徒在公元236年選舉的（優西比烏斯《教會史》第六章29.2-4）。迦太基的西普里安（公元258年）曾說到“全體信徒的選舉”（第六十七封書信.5；《尼西亞初期的教父》，第五冊第371頁）。《聖使徒章程》（可能寫於第四世紀）記載，教會的領袖需要由“全體信徒選舉”（第八章2.4；《尼西亞初期的教父》，第七冊第481頁）。從第四世紀開始，由附近的主教提名新主教，並由本教區的神職人員和平信徒批准通過，已成為既定的政策。在中世紀，平信徒當然是指貴族，而不是平民。
**長老。**參徒11:30註釋。藉著授於他們擔任傳道者的權力（見徒13:3），保羅和巴拿巴主持選立了長老。他們就這樣在外邦教會中制定了一種已為耶路撒冷的基督徒所接受的組織形式。那是以會堂為基礎，而不是以聖殿為基礎的（見《SDA聖經註釋》卷五第57頁）。當會堂的成員成為基督徒以後不久，保羅就組織了這些教會，這說明組織對於維持教會的屬靈生命和成長是很重要的。
**禁食禱告。**程序與使徒們自己在安提阿被分派的時候一樣（見徒13:3註釋）。
**交託。**說明一個人對另一個人的信任，把自己的財產交給他保管。該詞在本節暗示了對上帝的絕對信靠。

1.zh:
二人在以哥念同進猶太人的會堂，在那裡講的，叫猶太人和希利尼人信的很多。

**二人…同。**顯然不是指保羅和巴拿巴某一次進會堂與猶太人會面，而是指多次。
**以哥念。**保羅和巴拿巴前往以哥唸的旅程，路加只匆匆帶過，可能是因為路上沒有什麼工作的機會。以哥念位於安提阿東南約145公里，在幾條重要道路的交匯處。一些古代作者稱它屬弗呂家；還有一些稱它屬呂高尼。這個城市的面積和地位足可使它被稱為呂高尼的大馬士革，在後來基督教的傳說中以保羅和他所勸化的塞克拉的故事而聞名。在中世紀，以哥念上升為賽爾柱蘇丹的首都，使用另一個簡化了的名字科尼亞。至今它依然是土耳其的一座繁華的城市。見本卷註釋280，33頁地圖。
**進猶太人的會堂。**就像往常一樣，保羅開始在猶太人和敬畏上帝的外邦人中的工作，與他們在崇拜的地方見面。訪問這些會堂顯然在安息日（見徒13:14,44註釋）。
**在那裡講的。**他們多次講論。在場的有時不僅有猶太人，也有外邦人（見下面“希臘人”註釋）。
**希臘人。**Hellēnes，路加用該詞指外邦人，與Hellēnistai（講希臘語的猶太人）形成對照（見徒11:20註釋）。顯然這裡與安提阿一樣，有“相信”的外邦人進入會堂（參徒13:16）。再者，使徒們在以哥念停留了多日（見徒14:3），無疑還在會堂以外的地方傳福音。
**信的很多。**正如他們在敘利亞的安提阿講道一樣（見徒11:21,24），在這裡傳福音也取得了顯著的成功。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–3節）**。《使徒行述》第177頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（1–28節）**。《使徒行述》第177-188頁。

2.zh:
但那不順從的猶太人聳動外邦人，叫他們心裡惱恨弟兄。

**不順從的猶太人。**或“不信的猶太人”，說明不信導致背逆，準確描述了迫害保羅和巴拿巴的猶太人的品格。
**聳動外邦人。**《使徒行傳》所記載的大部分逼迫都是猶太人的敵意引起的。底米丟的事例（徒19:24）可能是唯一的例外。但即使在這件事上，猶太人似乎也對這個希臘工匠的惡毒反應負有責任。許久之後，約在公元二世紀後期，猶太人積極參與殺害士每拿的波利卡普（《坡旅甲的殉道》第13頁；優西比烏斯《教會史》第四章15.29）。公元三世紀初期，德爾圖良稱當時的猶太會堂為“迫害的源頭”（ Scorpiace10）.
**惱恨弟兄。**指新信徒，與“不順從的猶太人”形成對比。

3.zh:
二人在那裡住了多日，倚靠主放膽講道；主藉他們的手施行神蹟奇事，證明他的恩道。

**多日。**可能是幾個月。因為有許多新信徒，所以要在那裡停留許久，以堅固他們的信心。
**放膽講道。**他們的勇氣在於充分宣揚上帝恩典的福音，與皈依猶太教的外邦人所熟悉的狹隘的猶太教主義形成了鮮明的對比。見徒9:27-29。如此的膽量與神奇的行為，以及奉耶穌的名所行的其他神蹟奇事有密切的關係。
**神蹟奇事。**這不是信心的基礎，而是信心的憑據。這裡沒有具體說明所行的“神蹟”。
**證明。**衪藉著賜給保羅和巴拿巴能力施行神蹟，證明他們是衪的使者，傳揚衪的真理。
**衪的恩道。**指上帝救恩的信息，福音的快樂信息。保羅的講論總是述說上帝白白賜下的救恩（見弗2:5,8；羅5:1,2）。

4.zh:
城裡的眾人就分了黨，有附從猶太人的，有附從使徒的。

**分了黨。**在當地人中，基督徒和非基督徒明確地分成派別，非基督徒還懷著仇恨的精神。路加顯然是指大批的外邦人。皈依基督教的人無疑僅佔少數，並來自社會底層。這是初期教會的普遍現象（見林前1:26-28）。正如彼西底的安提阿那樣，城裡的權貴都反對他們（見徒13:50）。
**有附從猶太人的。**和後來保羅在帖撒羅尼迦傳道時一樣（徒17:4,5）。耶穌曾預言傳揚衪的道會導致這種分裂（路12:51-53）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第178頁。

5.zh:
那時，外邦人和猶太人，並他們的官長，一齊擁上來，要凌辱使徒，用石頭打他們。

**官長。**指保羅和巴拿巴開始在以哥念傳道時所進入的猶太會堂中的官長。
**擁上來。**hormē，“襲擊”或“攻擊”。不是直接襲擊，因為實際上並沒有發生（見第6節）。猶太人慫恿和煽動他們的異教同夥，希望發生暴力行為。
**要凌辱使徒。**他們遭遇蠻橫的侮辱和暴力。這說明所策劃的是暴民鬧事。保羅用一個極其相似的詞語描述他自己作為逼迫者的行為（提前1:13）。
**用石頭打他們。**石刑是猶太人懲罰褻瀆的手段（利24:14-16）。他們顯然認為使徒犯了褻瀆的罪。他們實施這些計劃，似乎沒有合法的手續；他們只是決定“凌辱使徒”（見徒7:58註釋；參約10:31）。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–6節）**。《使徒行述》第179頁。

6.zh:
使徒知道了，就逃往呂高尼的路司得、特庇兩個城和周圍地方去，

**知道了。**無疑有一些站在使徒一邊的人與反對派有密切的接觸，知道了他們的陰謀。路加沒有想誇張基督傳道士所受的苦難，對這次倖免於石刑只作了簡單的講述，沒有詳細刻畫。
**逃往。**使徒遵照耶穌的吩咐：“有人在這城逼迫你們，就逃到那城裡去”（見太10:23註釋）。
**呂高尼。**呂高尼不是一個羅馬行省，而是一個民族區域，西部屬羅馬的加拉太行省，東部屬於哥瑪基的安條克王國。保羅和巴拿巴顯然留在加拉太省境內。在《新約》時期，以哥念屬於弗呂家，因此使徒進入路司得和特庇，就算到了一個新的地區。
**路司得。**直到公元1885年才知道路司得的準確位置。那一年發現了一個碑銘，證明路司得就是現在的佐爾德。從以哥念向西南行駛，到這裡大約需要六個小時旅程。使徒們從以哥念出發，要爬過一些山，才到達路司得所在的高原。儘管在古典文學中呂高尼是一個野蠻未開化的地區，但碑銘的證據卻表明路司得在奧古斯都治下是羅馬的殖民地，無疑享有比周圍地區更高的文明。作為一個羅馬的商業中心，路司得的人口中必定有猶太人。但《使徒行傳》的記載並沒有提到這裡有猶太會堂；保羅似乎主要與外邦人接觸。甚至提摩太雖然有一個虔誠猶太母親，但他仍可能是路司得人，自小沒有受割禮（見徒16:1,3註釋）。見本卷註釋第280頁地圖。
**特庇。**特庇的地點是在1956年發現的。當時有一塊碑銘中提到在以哥念（現在的科尼埃）東南83公里處的克蒂許於克發現了特庇。近年發現了另一塊碑銘，確定了這個結論。後來與保羅同行的該猶，就是特庇人（徒20:4）。見本卷註釋第280頁地圖。
**周圍的地方。**說明路司得和特庇是小城市；保羅和巴拿巴在那裡傳道的時間很短。他們既在周圍的鄉村工作，所遇到的應該全是外邦人。

7.zh:
在那裡傳福音。

**傳福音。**euaggelizō（見徒13:32註釋）。

8.zh:
路司得城裡坐著一個兩腳無力的人，生來是瘸腿的，從來沒有走過。

**生來。**這是路加作為一名醫生記錄病情細節的一個例子（見徒3:7；9:33註釋）。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–10節）**。《早期著作》第203頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（8–13節）**。《使徒行述》第181頁。

9.zh:
他聽保羅講道，保羅定睛看他，見他有信心，可得痊癒，

**聽。**或“過去聽”。
**定睛看。**atenizō（見徒13:9；23:1註釋）。這位瘸腿之人的信心無疑在他的面容上表顯出來。保羅看到這個人的治癒，能成為路司得人眼前的神蹟。
**他有信心。**信心是醫治奇蹟的先決條件（見太9:22；可9:23）。

10.zh:
就大聲說：你起來，兩腳站直！那人就跳起來，而且行走。

**大聲說。**保羅提高了嗓門，超過他平時對百姓說話的聲音。
**兩腳站直。**凡沒有藉著信心預備好邁出常人經驗界限的人，會把這個吩咐當作嘲笑。這位瘸子願意憑著信心行事。這個神蹟與太9:6,7的癱子（太9:6,7），畢士大池子旁邊的瘸子（約5:11,14），以及美門口的瘸子（徒3:6-8）得醫治的情況相似，屬靈的恢復伴隨著身體的醫治。
保羅在路司得治癒瘸子，與彼得在聖殿美門口醫治瘸子（徒3:1-11）的情況相似。
**跳起來，而且行走。**或“跳起來，開始行走”（見徒3:8註釋）。

11.zh:
眾人看見保羅所做的事，就用呂高尼的話大聲說：有神藉著人形降臨在我們中間了。

**呂高尼的話。**雖然保羅說自己能講多種方言（林前14:18），但這種恩賜顯然並不包括明白呂高尼人的話。比較一致的意見是，他和巴拿巴不知道路司得人要拜他們。猜測他們故意讓百姓策劃把他們當作神來拜，以便在拒絕這種敬拜時表顯出戏劇性的效果，這並不符合他們的性格。路司得人無疑是懂兩種語言的。他們可以明白保羅和巴拿巴用希臘語說話。但當他們計劃舉行異教獻祭時，這兩位福音使者不能明白他們在說什麼。呂高尼語言的特徵我們不瞭解。
**神。**在《新約》時代，不僅呂高尼人，而且一般信奉異教的人，不論城裡的，還是鄉下的，都相信神明會這樣來到人間。在呂高尼有一個古老的神話，成為百姓試圖敬拜保羅和巴拿巴的依據。根據這個神話，宙斯和赫耳墨斯（朱庇特和墨丘利）化裝成人，受到老年夫婦腓力門和博西斯的款待；他們因此而獲得了報賞（《變形記》第八卷第626-724頁）。傳說中神明居住過的地方，後來成了虔誠的崇拜者敬拜的一個廟宇。他們來到這裡朝聖並獻上祭物。

12.zh:
於是稱巴拿巴為丟斯，稱保羅為希耳米，因為他說話領首。

**宙斯…希耳米。**Zeus… Hermēs。希臘的宙斯是眾神之主。他的兒子希耳米（赫耳墨斯），是諸神的傳令官和信使，也是口才的守護神。在羅馬的萬神殿中，這兩位神被稱為朱庇特和墨丘利。在路司得地區，敬拜宙斯和希耳米似乎十分盛行。在路司得附近發現了一個碑銘，上面記著一些呂高尼人的名字；他們把一座雕像獻給宙斯。在路司得附近還發現了一座石壇，獻與“祈禱的垂聽者”，可能就是宙斯和希耳米。路司得的百姓自然相信，若有神存有善意來到他們中間的話，那就一定是朱庇特；他們為朱庇特在城門建了神廟（見第13節註釋）。朱庇特是他們敬拜的主要對象。墨丘利被視為朱庇特的主要助手。巴拿巴給當地百姓的印象要比保羅更加深刻，所以被稱為朱庇特。保羅講得多，所以被稱為墨丘利。

13.zh:
有城外丟斯廟的祭司牽著牛，拿著花圈，來到門前，要同眾人向使徒獻祭。

**宙斯廟的祭司。**這句話的意思似乎是“城前當地宙斯廟的祭司”。所以說宙斯是路司得的守護神；宙斯的廟顯然就建在城門口，似乎在守護著城市。當地百姓呼喊著跑向宙斯廟的祭司，帶著獻祭所用的一切物品，前往使徒所居住房屋的門口。
**花圈。**在古代的雕塑中，這種花環十分常見，通常是白色羊毛製作的，有時還裝飾上樹葉和鮮花。祭司，侍從，門，祭壇，祭牲，通常都是這樣裝飾的。
**門前。**pulōnes，可以指房屋的門（見徒12:14），其他建築的門，或城門（見啟22:14）。一些人認為這裡是指保羅和巴拿巴所居住房屋的門。但理解為城門或宙斯廟宇的門可能更好（見上面“宙斯廟的祭司”註釋）。
**獻祭。**獻祭可能包括割斷牛的頸項，並把它們的血倒在壇上。
**懷愛倫註釋（13–15節）**。《早期著作》第203頁。

14.zh:
巴拿巴、保羅二使徒聽見，就撕開衣裳，跳進眾人中間，喊著說：

**巴拿巴、保羅二使徒。**獻祭的精心準備自然引起使徒的懷疑。
**撕開衣裳。**猶太人以此表示極其驚恐，尤其是表示對褻瀆話語的牴觸（見太26:65註釋）。保羅和巴拿巴意識到路司得的異教百姓即將在無知這中犯下這種罪。使徒的這種行動有多少為路司得百姓所理解，我們不得而知。但這如此烈的反應一定讓他們吃驚，並阻止了他們。
**跳進。**ekpēdaō，“跳出來”，“衝出”。門徒可能跑到城門口百姓聚集獻祭的地方，也許是“在城外”（見第13節註釋）宙斯的廟宇前。
**懷愛倫註釋（14–18節）**。《使徒行述》第182頁。

15.zh:
諸君，為什麼做這事呢？我們也是人，性情和你們一樣。我們傳福音給你們，是叫你們離棄這些虛妄，歸向那創造天、地、海、和其中萬物的永生神。

**性情和你們一樣。**該詞既表示通常所說的“性情”（見雅5:17），也涉及人類生活中比較消極的情感。保羅和巴拿巴這裡所說的話與彼得對哥尼流所說的話驚人地相似（徒10:26）。
**傳福音給你們。**直譯為“給你們帶來好信息”（見徒13:32註釋）。對於拜偶像的人來說，指出永生的上帝以代替不能言語的偶像，實在是“好消息”。特別是自從耶穌基督道成肉身，成為人類的救主以來。
**這些虛妄。**指即將發生的異教祭祀，以及一切含義。這樣的詞語常用來描述異教崇拜的空虛和無價值（弗4:17；彼前1:18）。
**天、地、海。**與外邦流行的宗教形成鮮明的對比，因為異教把天、地、海分為不同的神。保羅宣佈只有一位上帝創造了這一切並管理它們。
聖經經常提出上帝的創造。這是上帝與宇宙全部關係史的開端（創第1章），也是最後警告世界之福音的基礎（啟14:7）。
**永生上帝。**與他們的偶像崇拜形成對比。使徒呼籲路司得百姓歸向上帝。祂永遠活著，不斷行動，創造了天地，賜予一切美好的恩賜，必審判萬民。以賽亞曾強調這種對比（賽40:6-31；41:18-29；44:6-28）。

16.zh:
他在從前的世代，任憑萬國各行其道；

**萬國。**ethnē，《新約》常用該詞指外邦人。這裡第一次呈現了所謂保羅的歷史哲學。保羅在雅典的演講中也提出了相似的思想（徒17:30）。他說：“世人矇昧無知的時候，上帝並不監察”。生活在那時的人會受到公平的對待，根據他們有限的認識接受審判。他在羅1；2 中展開了這種哲學。外邦人的無知和罪惡會允許存在一段時間，作為上帝整體計劃的一部分，以便引導外邦人認識到救贖的需要，預備他們接受拯救。

17.zh:
然而為自己未嘗不顯出證據來，就如常施恩惠，從天降雨，賞賜豐年，叫你們飲食飽足，滿心喜樂。

**不顯出證據來。**在外邦人中，比如在路司得的外邦人中，上帝不會不留下見證。這又是一句綱要，以後將在羅1:19,20中展開，儘管他在那裡的觀點是外邦人沒有理由推委。在本節中，保羅強調上帝慈愛的證據顯在大自然中，是他的聽眾可以不斷看到的。後來保羅在對雅典的哲學家說話的時候，宣稱“我們生活、動作、存留都在乎祂”（徒17:28；參羅2:14,15）。
**常施恩惠。**說明祂為了人類不斷地彰顯祂慈愛的證據（見太5:45）。保羅提到了“從天降雨”，與被奉為雨神的朱庇特形成了對照。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第598頁；《教育論》第66頁；見羅1:20，21懷愛倫註釋。

18.zh:
二人說了這些話，僅僅的攔住眾人不獻祭與他們。

**僅僅地攔住。**百姓急於敬拜他們。一些人被阻止的人，無疑從“虛妄”轉向侍奉永生的上帝。保羅顯然在路司得工作到建立起一個教會。猶太人羅以和她的女兒友尼基，以及外孫提摩太肯定列在第一批信徒之中（提後1:5；見徒16:1註釋）。
**不獻祭。**指“放棄了獻祭”。

19.zh:
但有些猶太人從安提阿和以哥念來，挑唆眾人，就用石頭打保羅，以為他是死了，便拖到城外。

**猶太人從安提阿…來。**根據上下文，顯然是指彼西底的安提阿（見徒13:14註釋）。安提阿猶太人敵意之強烈，表現在安提阿和以哥念猶太人聯合行動，表現在安提阿的猶太人走了160多公里路，來阻撓使徒的工作。
在一座安提阿雕像上所發現的碑銘，說明了安提阿人和路司得人之間的密切關係。碑銘上說這座紀念的雕像是路司得人特為安提阿人建立起來的。
這些猶太人知道保羅和巴拿巴是他們的同族，就對他們怒火中燒，可能是因他們認為使徒取消了他們所如此看重的律法要求。然而這些在路司得控告的猶太人也許使用了其他的控詞，煽動外邦人反對使徒。醫治瘸子的神蹟證明了使徒能力的真實性，但沒有證明能力的來源。如今猶太人可能將之歸諸邪惡的勢力，以便影響外邦人（參耶穌的相同經歷，太12:24-27）。
**挑唆眾人。**路司得人態度的突然改變，就像耶路撒冷群眾的“和散那”轉變為“把祂釘十字架”那樣（太21:9；27:22）。像呂高尼人這樣迷信的群眾情緒變幻無常是不難理解的。他們素來被稱為靠不住的人。在馬耳他的異教居民中，也有過相似的態度轉變，但方向是相反的（徒28:3-6）。路司得的百姓推測，既然保羅和巴拿巴擁有如此神奇的能力，而又不是化為人形的神，那麼他們必定是巫師，甚至可能是魔鬼。猶太人可能煽起這種情緒，唆使百姓採取野蠻的行動。
**用石頭打保羅。**這是猶太人的懲罰方式。猶太人無疑是煽動者，又得到路司得居民的幫助。保羅生涯中受這種形式的迫害，這是記錄下來的一次（見林後11:25）。在以哥念，保羅剛剛逃過了猶太人的石頭（徒14:5,6）。這兩件事路加都有記錄，但是使徒只一次提到自己被石頭砸。路司得的這次經歷在保羅的記憶中十分清晰，直至他生命的最後（提後3:11,12）。
**拖到城外。**希伯來人的律法規定，石刑要在營外或城外執行（利24:14）。但由於路司得是一個外邦城市，石刑是暴徒行為的結果，石刑似乎是在城裡發生的。所以保羅的身體被拖到城外。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《使徒行述》第183頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（19–20節）**。《使徒行述》第184頁；《早期著作》第203頁。

20.zh:
門徒正圍著他，他就起來，走進城去。第二天，同巴拿巴往特庇去，

**門徒。**指新信徒。他們顯然無法預先阻止襲擊，但他們跟到保羅受難的地方，看到他不醒人事，被人拖著，心裡十分悲傷，可能在想如何舉行恭敬的葬禮。我們有理由相信提摩太目睹使徒被石頭砸（見《使徒行述》184，185頁）。保羅痛苦的經歷對於他來說既是服務的挑戰，也是獻身的榜樣。羅以和友尼基可能也在人群中，先是悲哀，後因發現自己敬愛的老師沒有死而高興。
**他就起來。**保羅從昏迷中醒來，馬上熱情勇敢地回城，應該被看作一個奇蹟。一人被兇殘的暴徒用石頭所砸，以為死了而被拖到城外的人，居然醒了，而且行若無事地行走，這是上帝能力的證據，比癱子痊癒更令人矚目。
**第二天。**儘管保羅在上帝的保佑下倖免於難，但他意識到百姓的態度並沒有改變，因此最好暫時離開那座城市。他後來至少兩次去訪問路司得（見第21節；徒16:1）。
**同巴拿巴。**巴拿巴沒有特別受猶太人所嫉恨。儘管他是大有能力的“勸慰子”或“安慰者”（見徒4:36註釋），但他的能力顯然不如他的同工保羅。
**往特庇去。**見第6節註釋。

21.zh:
對那城裡的人傳了福音，使好些人作門徒，就回路司得、以哥念、安提阿去，

**傳了福音。**euaggelizō （見徒13:32註釋）。
**使好些人作門徒。**也許特庇的該猶是路加所提到保羅第二次傳道旅程的同伴（見徒20:4）。該猶可能是這時悔改的。使徒所成就的工作說明他們在那裡逗留了好幾個月時間。
**就回。**向東前往大數，和乘船回敘利亞的安提阿要容易得多。但保羅和巴拿巴選擇了一條又長又疲憊的路。返回大海的路約有402公里。但是從原路返回，他們就有機會進一步播撒他們早先冒著個人生命危險所撒的真理種子。安提阿和以哥念猶太人的敵意一定減弱了，所以使徒們能重新訪問這些城市而沒有生命的危險。也許一些地方的城市官員任期已滿，由其他人接替。見本卷註釋280頁地圖。
**懷愛倫註釋（21–23節）**。《使徒行述》第185頁。

22.zh:
堅固門徒的心，勸他們恆守所信的道；又說：我們進入神的國，必須經歷許多艱難。

**堅固。**或“加強”。這並不是指以後教會所常用的堅信禮。保羅這裡的行動與耶穌對彼得的告誡一致：“你回頭以後，要堅固你的弟兄”（路22:32）。保羅可以根據自己的試煉和如何從試煉中得救而進行警告和勸勉。
**所信的道。**指所信所傳的道，還出現在以後的使徒書信中（見提後4:7；猶3,20），意思可能相同。
**我們。**這句話顯然直接引自保羅在這次訪問中對教會所說的話。有人認為，路加用了“我們”表明他本人也在場聽講道。然而鑑於直到保羅第二次傳道旅程到特羅亞時，才提到旅行的同人（徒16:10），我們最好把這裡的“我們”理解為保羅的原話；他把自己與聽眾視為一體。他當然可以用自己所受的苦難，來說明他信息的真理。
**上帝的國。**見徒1:6註釋。福音書常使用該詞。它出現得很早，常出現在保羅教訓的記錄中（羅14:17；林前4:20；6:9；西4:11；帖後1:5）。對於保羅來說，這是一個真實的國度；基督是君王。
**必須經歷許多艱難。**保羅在寫給路司得所召選的門徒提摩太的第二封書信中（見徒16:1-3），述說了感人的苦難經歷。他提到了自己在安提阿，路司得和以哥念所受的迫害，並發表了一條格言：“凡立志在基督耶穌裡敬虔度日的，都要受逼迫”（提後3:12；參啟1:9；7:14）。

24.zh:
二人經過彼西底，來到旁非利亞。

**彼西底。**見徒13:14註釋。
**旁非利亞。**見徒13:13註釋。
**懷愛倫註釋（24–26節）**。《使徒行述》第187頁。

25.zh:
在別加講了道，就下亞大利去，

**別加。**馬可就是從這個城市離開的（徒13:13）。沒有提到使徒們以前曾在這裡傳道。如今他們回來了，做他們以前顯然沒有做的工作。
**亞大利。**在進入該省的路上，使徒們顯然是直接從帕弗到了別加，沿塞斯特魯斯河而上（見徒13:13註釋）。他們在返回的時候，繞道來到亞大利。這是卡塔爾哈茨河的一個港口。這座城市是別迦摩國王阿塔羅斯二世建造的（公元前159-138年）。沒有任何在亞大利工作的記錄。使徒可能只是來到這裡的港口，乘船前往敘利亞。見本卷註釋280頁地圖。

26.zh:
從那裡坐船，往安提阿去。當初，他們被眾人所託、蒙神之恩，要辦現在所做之工，就是在這地方。

**安提阿。**指敘利亞的安提阿。使徒們從這裡出發。他們的船可能穿過基利家和塞浦路斯之間，要麼在西流基靠岸，要麼進入奧龍特斯河駛往安提阿。
**所託。**安提阿教會在派遣保羅和巴拿巴的時候，將他們交託上帝的恩典，在工作中引領，保守和支持他們。
**他們…辦…所做之工。**保羅和巴拿巴奉安提阿教會委託去執行一項特殊的任務──傳福音給外邦人。如今他們可以心滿意足地返回自己的教會，因為他們的任務完成了。雖然他們才開始對外邦人傳道，卻做得很好。

28.zh:
二人就在那裡同門徒住了多日。

**多日。**對於保羅來說，安提阿自然比耶路撒冷吸引力更大，因為在這裡首先建立了外邦人的教會，又是該教會任命他為外邦人的傳道士。在這段時間裡，兩位使徒無疑繼續吸引許多外邦人信主，除了先前悔改的外邦人以外。

39.en: We are witnesses. Peter had been with Jesus from the beginning of His ministry (John 1:40–42). The apostle recognized that the main purpose of his mission was to witness for Christ to men, as the Lord had commanded (see Acts 1:8, 21, 22; cf. Matt. 28:19, 20; Luke 24:48). Land. Gr. chōra, “region,” “countryside,” here contrasted with the city, Jerusalem (see Luke 2:8; Acts 26:20). They slew and hanged. See on ch. 5:30. As in ch. 2:23, Peter represents the crucifixion as mainly the act of the rulers and people of Jerusalem, and not of the Roman governor. Tree. Gr. xulon, “wood,” but used in the LXX and the papyri also for “tree.” Clearly the cross is meant. There does not appear to be any allusion here to the tree of knowledge of good and evil in Eden, as some commentators have suggested.
39.zh:
他在猶太人之地，並耶路撒冷所行的一切事，有我們作見證。他們竟把他掛在木頭上殺了。

**地。**chōra，“地區”，“院子”，與耶路撒冷相對應（見路2:8；徒26:20）。
**有我們作見證。**從耶穌開始工作時起，彼得就跟隨祂了（約1:40-42）。使徒意識到自己使命的主要目的，就是遵照主的吩咐，向世人見證基督（見徒1:8,21,22；參太28:19,20；路24:48）。
**他們竟把祂掛在木頭上殺了。**見徒5:30註釋。和徒2:23一樣，彼得稱耶穌被釘主要是耶路撒冷的官長和百姓所為，而不是羅馬巡撫所為。
**木頭。**xulon，但是在七十士譯本和蒲紙文獻中也表示“樹”。這裡顯然是指十字架，不像一些註釋家所認為的，是指伊甸園中的分別善惡樹。

9.en: Drew nigh. The events that led to Peter’s vision were so timed as to bring the climax of that vision just at the hour the messengers arrived (see vs. 17–20). Housetop. Gr. dōma, “building,” “house.” To “go up on the house” was to ascend to the housetop, which in the East was usually flat. This was an appropriate place for prayer and meditation. In a city like Joppa, and in the tanner’s house, it was perhaps the only place suitable for such a purpose. For examples of other uses of housetops see 1 Sam. 9:25; Jer. 19:13; Matt. 10:27. The sixth hour. That is, midday. Among the Jews this probably was not one of the regular hours for prayer, and early Jewish literature says nothing about it as such. Particularly pious persons may have observed it (see Ps. 55:17), and Peter’s prayer at this hour may possibly be so interpreted (see on Acts 3:1). However, other explanations are also possible. The regular morning prayer, which normally took place about 9:00 A.M., at the time of the morning offering, might be offered as late as noon. Thus it may have been his morning prayer that Peter was offering. Another other interesting possibility is suggested by a Jewish regulation that goes back at least to the 3d century A.D. This rule provided that if a man had not eaten until midday, he should then first offer his afternoon prayer before partaking of food, for the afternoon prayer (normally about 3:00 P.M.) was not to be said soon after eating. Inasmuch as Peter was “very hungry” (ch. 10:10), it may have been that on the day in question he had not yet eaten, and so purposely offered his evening prayer at an earlier hour. Whatever explanation is adopted for Peter’s having prayed at this hour, it is clear that his meditation and devotion opened the way for his reception of a vision at exactly the right moment to prepare him to receive the messengers from the Gentile Cornelius.
9.zh:
第二天，他們行路將近那城。彼得約在午正，上房頂去禱告，

**將近。**導致彼得見異象的事件，時間都是安排好的。使者們來到時，異象正達到高潮（見第17-20節）。
**午正。**指中午。在猶太人中，這可能不是猶太人定期禱告的時辰。早期猶太人文獻中沒有提到這個禱告的時辰。特別虔誠的人可能遵守這個時辰（見詩55:17）。彼得在這個時辰的祈禱可以這樣解釋（見徒3:1註釋）。但也可能有其他的解釋。常規的晨禱通常是在上午九點，是獻早祭的時候，可能會推到正午舉行。所以這可能是彼得在進行晨禱。另一種有趣的解釋源於一條猶太人的規則。這條規則至少可以追溯到公元三世紀。即如果一個人在正午前沒有吃東西，那他在吃東西之前應先獻上下午的祈禱，因為下午的祈禱（通常在下午三點左右）不應在飯後馬上進行。鑑於彼得“餓了”（徒10:10），那一天他可能還沒有吃東西，所以故意將傍晚的禱告提前了。
不論怎麼解釋彼得此時的禱告，他的默想和虔誠顯然為他在合適的時間見異象開了路，預備他接待百夫長哥尼流的使者。
**房頂。**dōma，“樓房”，“房屋”。彼得“上房頂去禱告”。東方的屋頂通常是平的。這是祈禱默想的理想地點。在約帕這樣的城市，在硝皮匠的家裡，這大概是唯一適合禱告的地點了。有關屋頂其他用途的例子，見撒上9:25；耶19:13；太10:27。
**懷愛倫註釋（9–16節）**。《使徒行述》第135頁。

4.en: Looked. Or, “gazed intently,” “stared.” He was afraid. The angel is called a “man … in bright clothing” (v. 30; cf. ch. 1:10). For the moment his sudden appearance terrorized Cornelius. The Roman soldiers guarding the tomb of Christ, who were not attuned spiritually as was Cornelius, shook and became like dead men in the presence of the blazing glory of the resurrection angel (see Matt. 28:2, 4; cf. Dan. 10:7–11). What is it? By this question Cornelius indicated that the vision involved more than he could understand, and his words may be taken to imply his readiness to follow divine direction. Compare the response Saul gave when Christ appeared to him on the road near Damascus (ch. 9:6). Lord. Gr. kurios, a title of respect, which, when applied to human beings, is to be translated, “sir” (ch. 16:30), but when referred to God, means “Lord” (ch. 7:33). Which translation is preferable here depends on the degree to which Cornelius at first recognized the angel as a heavenly messenger. “Lord” is probably the better translation. Thy prayers and thine alms. See on v. 2. Cornelius’ alms were a tangible expression of the sincerity of his inner spiritual life, nourished, as it was, by habitual prayer. Are come up. Rather, “have arisen.” Prayer may be thought of as similar to incense ascending to the throne of God (see Rev. 5:8; 8:3, 4) or to the smoke of the burnt offering, which in Hebrew was called an ‘olah, “that which ascends.” This was a particularly fitting expression to use for prayer offered at the time of the evening sacrifice (see on Acts 10:3). Memorial. Gr. mnēmosunon, a word used repeatedly in the LXX to refer to the portion of the meal offering the priest burned upon the altar (Lev. 2:2, 9, 16; 5:12; 6:15). The smoke of the offering, as it ascended, was representative of Israel’s prayers. This same word appears in Tobit 12:12, where an angel says, “I did bring the memorial of your prayer before the glory of the Lord” (in R. H. Charles, The Apocrypha and Pseudepigrapha of the Old Testament, vol. 1, p. 234). The prayers of Cornelius were acceptable to God. He followed “the true Light, which lighteth every man” (John 1:9), and he partook of the faith that from the beginning of the world has opened the way to justification—the belief that the true God “is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him” (Heb. 11:6).
4.zh:
哥尼流定睛看他，驚怕說：主啊，什麼事呢？天使說：你的禱告和你的賙濟達到神面前，已蒙記唸了。

**驚怕。**聖經說天使“穿著光明的衣服”（第30節；參徒1:10）。他的突然顯現使哥尼流十分害怕。守衛基督墳墓的羅馬士兵，屬靈的狀況不像哥尼流。他們在復活的使者耀眼的光芒面前，嚇得渾身發抖，甚至像死人一樣（見太28:2,4；參但10:7-11）。
**主啊。**kurios，這是一個尊稱，在指人時應譯為“先生”（徒16:30），指上帝時，意思就是“主”（徒7:33）。這裡採用哪一種譯法，取決於哥尼流對天使身份的最初認定。譯為“主”可能較好。
什麼事呢？哥尼流的這個問題說明他對異象不太明白，也說明他願意接受上帝的引導。參基督在在快到大馬士革的路上向掃羅顯現時，掃羅的回答（徒9:6）。
**你的禱告和你的賙濟。**見第2節註釋。哥尼流的賙濟表明他內心屬靈生命的真實性；他習慣性的祈禱維持了他的屬靈生命。
**達到。**或“上升”。祈禱可以被視為如同上升到上帝寶座的香（參啟5:8；8:3,4），或希伯來語中被稱為`olah的燔祭“上升”的煙。這是表達晚祭時所獻上祈禱的非常合適的詞（見徒10:3註釋）。
**記念。**mnēmosunon，在七十士譯本中經常使用，指祭司燒在壇上的素祭的一部分（利2:2,9,16；5:12；6:15）。祭物上升的煙，代表以色列人的祈禱。該詞還出現在《多比傳》12:12中。該節有一位天使說：“是我將你禱告傳達到上帝的寶座前”（R. H. 查爾斯，《舊約次經與偽經》卷一第234頁）。哥尼流的禱告蒙上帝悅納。他順從了那“真光，照亮一切生在地上的人”（約1:9），接受了從世界之初就敞開稱義之路的信仰，相信“有上帝，且信祂賞賜那尋求祂的人”（來11:6）。
**懷愛倫註釋**。《證言》卷三第405頁；《證言》卷七第216頁。
**懷愛倫註釋（4–6節）**。《救贖的故事》第283頁。

42.en: Commanded us to preach. This command is implied in Matt. 28:18–20, and is covered by the instruction in Acts 1:8 to witness concerning the kingdom of God (cf. ch. 1:2). Ordained of God. Under the terms of the everlasting covenant Christ was to accomplish man’s salvation. This makes it fitting that He also should be the judge of men, in complete fulfillment of the covenant. Quick. That is, “living.” Paul (ch. 17:31) agrees with Peter in connecting the resurrection with the assurance that He who had risen was to be the future judge of all men. The fact that Jesus was a man, and yet a man who was victorious over sin and death, and the further fact that at the same time He was God, the author of the law by which men are judged, make Him the logical and rightful one to be the judge of all men (see on John 5:22, 27).
42.zh:
他吩咐我們傳道給眾人，證明他是神所立定的，要作審判活人、死人的主。

**吩咐我們傳。**這個吩咐包含在太28:18-20 和徒1:8 的指示中，就是為上帝的國作見證（參徒1:2）。
**上帝所立定。**根據永約的條款，基督要成就人類的救贖。這使祂也適於擔任人類的審判者，完全成就聖約。
**活人。**保羅（徒17:31）贊同彼得把復活作為復活的主將來審判萬民的保證。耶穌是人，是戰勝死亡和罪惡的人，同時祂也是上帝，是立法者，人要根據這部律法接受審判，所以祂理當成為萬民的審判者（見約5:22,27註釋）。

41.en: Not to all. The Jews in general, having failed to recognize Jesus as the Messiah foretold in OT prophecy, were not likely to be willing witnesses to His resurrection (see Luke 16:31). The fact that even some of the disciples were at first unprepared to accept the risen Christ (Matt. 28:17; Mark 16:14) illustrates how unavailing a public appearance to the Jews in general would have been. Witnesses chosen before. The disciples had been chosen from the beginning not only to aid Jesus in His ministry but, even more, to be witnesses after His departure to what they had seen and heard (see Matt. 28:19, 20; John 17:6–8; Acts 1:8; 2 Peter 1:16–18). To us. See Acts 1:3; 1 Cor. 15:5–8. Did eat and drink. See Luke 24:42, 43; John 21:13–15. His eating and drinking was the crucial test that proved Christ was no phantom of the disciples’ imagination.
41.zh:
不是顯現給眾人看，乃是顯現給神預先所揀選為他作見證的人看，就是我們這些在他從死裡復活以後和他同吃同喝的人。

**不是顯現給眾人看。**猶太人一般沒有認出耶穌就是《舊約》所預言的彌賽亞，所以他們不可能願意見證耶穌的復活（見路16:31）。甚至一些門徒起先也沒有準備好接受復活的基督（太28:17；可16:14）。這說明耶穌即便在猶太人中公開露面也是沒有效果的。
**預先所揀選為祂作見證的人。**門徒從一開始就蒙揀選，不僅協助耶穌傳道，而且在耶穌離開之後，見證他們所看到、所聽到的事（見太28:19,20；約17:6-8；徒1:8；彼後1:16-18）。
**我們。**見徒1:3；林前15:5-8.
**同吃同喝。**見路24:42,43；約21:13-15。基督的吃與喝乃是重要的證據，證明祂不是門徒想象中的幻影。

6.en: Simon a tanner. See on ch. 9:43. He shall tell thee. Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the omission of the words, “he shall tell thee what thou oughtest to do.” However, the same thought is set forth in Peter’s own account of the visit to Cornelius (ch. 11:14), in the clause, “who shall tell thee words, whereby thou and all thy house shall be saved.” This is one of several instances found in some late manuscripts of the Acts where apparently an endeavor has been made to form a complete narrative in the earlier chapters by gathering together and adapting statements that appeared originally only in later chapters (cf. ch. 9:6). For a discussion of the status of full proselytes and “proselytes of the gate,” who had accepted the Jewish faith in part, see Vol. V, p. 62.
6.zh:
他住在海邊一個硝皮匠西門的家裡，房子在海邊上。

**硝皮匠西門。**見徒9:43註釋。有文本在本節的最後還有“他會告訴你應該做什麼”。在彼得自己敘述會見哥尼流的話中有這樣的意思：“他有話要告訴你，可以使你和你的全家得救” （徒11:14）。這說明《使徒行傳》一些後來的文稿曾試圖把前幾章的敘述補充得完整一些，就把後幾章的句子插了進去（參徒9:6）。
關於完全皈依猶太教的人，和部分接受猶太人教信仰的“門口皈依者”，見本卷註釋第62頁。

48.en: Commanded them to be baptized. The construction seems to imply that Peter himself did not baptize these converts. Jesus (John 4:1, 2) and Paul (1 Cor. 1:14–16) refrained from baptizing converts, and apparently Peter followed a similar course in this instance. Paul declares that he refrained generally from baptizing, lest factions arise and Christian unity be broken by men dividing into parties under the names of those who had baptized them. This may also have been the reason here (see 1 Cor. 1:12). Who administered the baptism we are not told. Perhaps it was done by Peter’s companions. Possibly there already may have been an organized congregation at Caesarea, as the result of Philip’s work, and its elders or deacons, or Philip himself, may have acted under Peter’s instructions. The Lord. Textual evidence attests (cf. p. 10) the reading “Jesus Christ.” To tarry. It is probable that Peter consented to stay (see ch. 11:3), and thus showed that he was prepared to act thereafter according to the teaching of his vision. Peter must have mingled freely with the new converts, eating and drinking with them (vs. 2, 3) without fear of being defiled thereby. Luke gives so much space to Peter’s experience in Caesarea that it must be considered as marking a turning point in the life of the apostle, attesting his essential agreement with Paul. Although afterward Peter wavered in his attitude toward Gentile Christians (Gal. 2:11–13), and was rebuked by Paul for so doing, the account of that severe rebuke shows that Peter had laid aside his Jewish prejudices to a great degree, and had acted as he did only under the influence of certain very strict Jews who had come from Jerusalem to Antioch. Certain days. See on ch. 9:19.
48.zh:
就吩咐奉耶穌基督的名給他們施洗。他們又請彼得住了幾天。

**吩咐…給他們施洗。**本節的結構似乎暗示，彼得自己沒有給這些信徒施洗。耶穌（約4:1,2）和保羅（林前1:14-16）通常不給信徒施洗。彼得顯然這一次也如此行。保羅說自己一般不施洗，是為了避免結黨，使教會的團結遭到破壞，結果按施洗者的名字分成派別。這也可能是彼得如此行的原因（見林前1:12）。
聖經沒有告訴我們是誰執行洗禮。也許是由彼得的同伴施行的。可能由於腓利工作的結果，在凱撒利亞已經建立起教會組織。這裡的長老，執事，甚至腓利本人，可能都聽從彼得的“吩咐”。
**耶穌基督。**有文本為“主”。
**住了。**彼得可能同意留下（見徒11:3），從而表明他願意今後實行他異像的教訓。他一定與新信徒自由交往，一起吃喝（徒11:2,3），並不擔心遭到玷汙。路加對彼得在凱撒利亞經歷的大量描述，一定視之為使徒生活的一個轉折點，證明了他與保羅基本上一致。儘管後來彼得動搖了自己對於外邦基督徒的態度（加2:11-13），受到保羅的指責，那次嚴厲指責的記錄，證明彼得在很大的程度上已放棄了他的猶太人偏見，只是在一些從耶路撒冷到安提阿來的非常嚴格的猶太人影響之下，才這麼做的。
**幾天。**見徒9:19註釋。

40.en: The third day. This is an example of inclusive reckoning of a time period. For further discussion of this method see Vol. I, p. 182; Vol. II, pp. 136, 137; Vol. V, pp. 249, 250; cf. on v. 30. For the length of time Christ was in the tomb see Matt. 16:21; Luke 23:53 to 24:6. Shewed him openly. Literally, “gave Him to be manifest,” that is, “made Him manifest.” Christ was not openly shown (see v. 41), but by many proofs it was made clear to those who saw Him that He was the same Jesus, now alive and glorified, who had hung on the cross.
40.zh:
第三日，神叫他復活，顯現出來；

**第三日。**這是包括首尾的計時法。詳見《SDA聖經註釋》卷一第182頁；卷二第136,137頁；卷五第249,250頁；參第30節註釋。關於基督在墳墓裡的時間，見太16:21；路23:53 至24:6。
**叫祂復活，顯現。**基督沒有公開顯現（見第41節），但是許多證據證明，那些見過祂的人都很清楚，曾被釘在十字架上的同一位耶穌，如今活著並得了榮耀。

5.en: Send men. God willed that Cornelius should make an active effort to obtain knowledge of the gospel. Truths gained as the result of personal inquiry often are more preciously treasured than those that are urged upon us. Call for one Simon. Doubtless the centurion could have discovered that Simon the apostle was staying with Simon the tanner. But God, the Omniscient One, knew where Peter was and directed Cornelius accordingly. In His omniscience God knows every intimate detail about each one. Man’s realization of this can be a deterrent from sin; better, it is a vast encouragement to godly living. The psalmist’s wanderings and accompanying sorrows were known to God (Ps. 56:8). Even the fall of the sparrow is noted by the Lord, and the hairs of men’s heads are numbered (Matt. 10:29–31). The parallel between the experience of Cornelius and that of Ananias and Saul (Acts 9:10–12) is notable.
5.zh:
現在你當打發人往約帕去，請那稱呼彼得的西門來。

**打發人。**上帝希望哥尼流作出主動的努力，去領受福音的知識。通過個人的追求而得到的真理，往往比強加於我們的東西更受我們珍視。
**請那稱呼彼得的西門來。**百夫長無疑能查到使徒西門住在硝皮匠西門家裡。然而無所不知的上帝知道彼得在什麼地方，並給予哥尼流相應的指示。上帝憑著祂的全智，知道每一個人最詳盡的細節。意識到這一點，會使人不敢犯罪，並極大地鼓勵人過敬虔的生活。詩人說“我幾次流淚，你都記數”（詩56:8）。連一隻麻雀落下也受上帝關注。人的頭髮祂也數算過了（太10:29-31）。哥尼流的經歷與亞拿尼亞和掃羅的經歷（徒9:10-12）十分相似。
**懷愛倫註釋（5–8節）**。《使徒行述》第134頁。

10.en: Very hungry. Apparently Peter was not fasting, for he intended to eat. His noonday hunger prepared him for the command to eat, which was to be given him in connection with his vision (v. 13). Coming under these circumstances, the command was particularly forceful. Would have eaten. Literally, “was wishing to eat,” or “began to want to eat.” A trance. Gr. ekstasis, “a standing aside,” and by extension, a displacement of the mind from its normal environment. The English word “ecstasy” is derived from ekstasis. Luke uses this word again for Paul’s vision in the Temple (ch. 22:17). This word is employed in the LXX to describe the deep sleep of Abraham (Gen. 15:12). It represents a state in which the normal action of the senses is suspended, so that the vision is seen only mentally, as in a dream (see 2 Cor. 12:3). Peter’s ekstasis provided a channel for a revelation of the divine will.
10.zh:
覺得餓了，想要吃。那家的人正預備飯的時候，彼得魂遊象外，

**覺得餓了。**顯然彼得沒有在禁食，因為他打算去吃飯。他正午的飢餓為異象中叫他吃東西的命令做了準備（第13節）。命令在這種情況下特別有力。
**想要吃。**“正想吃”，“開始想吃”。
**魂遊象外。**ekstasis，“站在一旁”，引申為思想從正常的狀態下轉移。英語“ecstasy”（入迷）就源於ekstasis。路加還用該詞描述保羅在聖殿中所見的異象（徒22:17）。七十士譯本用該詞描述亞伯拉罕的沉睡（創15:12）。它表示一種正常的感官功能暫時中止的狀態。因此異像只能在意識中看到，就像在夢中（見林後12:3）。彼得的ekstasis為上帝旨意的啟示提供了通道。

1.en: Cæsarea. That is, Caesarea Palestinae, situated on the Mediterranean coast, not Caesarea Philippi. It was the capital of the Roman province (see on ch. 8:40) and the usual residence of the Roman procurator of Judea. It was doubtless a cosmopolitan city and a center of commerce. See Ministry of Peter to the Jews and Gentiles. Cornelius. Luke may have learned the details of this story during one of his stays at Caesarea (chs. 21:8; 23:33; 24:27). The conversion of Cornelius marks a new stage of expansion in the growth of the church. Cornelius was a Roman officer, but he was not completely a heathen. He was “devout” and “feared God,” and gave alms to the people (see on ch. 10:2). Even so, in Jewish eyes he was a Gentile, for he was uncircumcised.
